losetup.text:
4mLOSETUP24m(8)                              System Administration                             4mLOSETUP24m(8)

1mNAME0m
     losetup - set up and control loop devices

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     Set up a loop device:

     1mlosetup 22m[options] 1m-f22m|4mloopdev24m 4mfile0m

     Get info:

     1mlosetup 22m[1m-l22m] [1m-a22m|4mloopdev24m]

     1mlosetup -j 4m22mfile24m [1m-o 4m22moffset24m]

     Recalibrate the size of a loop device:

     1mlosetup -c 4m22mloopdev0m

     Detach loop devices:

     1mlosetup -d 4m22mloopdev24m ...

     1mlosetup -D0m

     Prevent loop devices from getting listed:

     1mlosetup --remove 4m22mloopdev24m ...

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     1mlosetup  22mis  used to associate loop devices with regular files or block devices, to detach loop
     devices, and to query the status of a loop device. If only the 4mloopdev24m argument is  given,  the
     status  of  the corresponding loop device is shown. If no option is given, all loop devices are
     shown.

     Note that the old output format (i.e., 1mlosetup -a22m) with comma-delimited strings  is  deprecated
     in favour of the 1m--list 22moutput format.

     It  is  possible  to  create  multiple independent loop devices for the same backing file. 1mThis0m
     1msetup may be dangerous, can cause data loss, corruption, and overwrites. 22mUse  1m--nooverlap  22mwith
     1m--find 22mduring setup to avoid this problem.

     The  loop  device  setup is not an atomic operation when used with 1m--find22m, and 1mlosetup 22mdoes not
     protect this operation by any lock. The number of attempts is internally restricted to a  maxi‐
     mum of 16. It is recommended to use for example 1mflock22m(1) to avoid a collision in heavily paral‐
     lel use cases.

1mOPTIONS0m
     The  4msize24m  and 4moffset24m arguments may be followed by the multiplicative suffixes KiB (=1024), MiB
     (=1024*1024), and so on for GiB, TiB, PiB, EiB, ZiB and YiB (the "iB" is  optional,  e.g.,  "K"
     has  the  same meaning as "KiB") or the suffixes KB (=1000), MB (=1000*1000), and so on for GB,
     TB, PB, EB, ZB and YB.

     1m-a22m, 1m--all0m
         Show the status of all loop devices. Note  that  not  all  information  is  accessible  for
         non-root  users. See also 1m--list22m. The old output format (as printed without 1m--list22m) is dep‐
         recated.

     1m-d22m, 1m--detach 4m22mloopdev24m...
         Detach the file or device associated with the specified loop  device(s).  Note  that  since
         Linux  v3.7  kernel  uses  "lazy  device destruction". The detach operation does not return
         1mEBUSY 22merror anymore if device is actively used by system, but it  is  marked  by  autoclear
         flag  and destroyed later. Even if the device is not used, the loop device can be destroyed
         later. If you need to wait for a complete removal of the loop device, call  1mudevadm  settle0m
         after 1mlosetup22m.

     1m-D22m, 1m--detach-all0m
         Detach all associated loop devices.

     1m-f22m, 1m--find 22m[4mfile24m]
         Find  the  first unused loop device. If a 4mfile24m argument is present, use the found device as
         loop device. Otherwise, just print its name.

     1m--show0m
         Display the name of the assigned loop device if the 1m-f  22moption  and  a  4mfile24m  argument  are
         present.

     1m-L22m, 1m--nooverlap0m
         Check  for  conflicts between loop devices to avoid situation when the same backing file is
         shared between more loop devices. If the file is already used by another device then re-use
         the device rather than a new one. The option makes sense only with 1m--find22m.

     1m-j22m, 1m--associated 4m22mfile24m [1m-o 4m22moffset24m]
         Show the status of all loop devices associated with the given 4mfile24m.

     1m-o22m, 1m--offset 4m22moffset0m
         The data start is moved 4moffset24m bytes into the specified file or device. The 4moffset24m  may  be
         followed by the multiplicative suffixes; see above.

     1m--loop-ref 4m22mstring0m
         Set  the reference string. The backwardly compatible default is to use the backing filename
         as a reference in the loop setup ioctl (aka lo_file_name). This option overrides  this  de‐
         fault  behavior and sets the reference to the 4mstring24m. The reference may be used by udevd in
         /dev/loop/by-ref. The Linux kernel does not use the reference at all, but it could be  used
         by  some  old utils that cannot read the backing file from sysfs. The reference is readable
         only for the root user (see 1m--output 22m+REF) and it is restricted to 64 bytes.

     1m--sizelimit 4m22msize0m
         The data end is set to no more than 4msize24m bytes after the data start. The 4msize24m may  be  fol‐
         lowed by the multiplicative suffixes; see above.

     1m-b22m, 1m--sector-size 4m22msize0m
         Set  the logical sector size of the loop device in bytes (since Linux 4.14). The option may
         be used when creating a new loop device as well as a stand-alone command to  modify  sector
         size of the already existing loop device.

     1m-c22m, 1m--set-capacity 4m22mloopdev0m
         Force the loop driver to reread the size of the file associated with the specified loop de‐
         vice.

     1m-P22m, 1m--partscan0m
         Force  the kernel to scan the partition table on a newly created loop device. Note that the
         partition table parsing depends on sector sizes. The default is sector size is  512  bytes,
         otherwise you need to use the option 1m--sector-size 22mtogether with 1m--partscan22m.

     1m-r22m, 1m--read-only0m
         Set up a read-only loop device.

     1m--direct-io22m[1m=on22m|1moff22m]
         Enable  or  disable  direct I/O for the backing file. The default is 1moff22m. Specifying either
         1m--direct-io 22mor 1m--direct-io=on 22mwill enable it. But, 1m--direct-io=off 22mcan be provided  to  ex‐
         plicitly turn it off.

     1m-l22m, 1m--list0m
         If  a  loop  device or the 1m-a 22moption is specified, print the default columns for either the
         specified loop device or all loop devices; the default is to print info about all  devices.
         See also 1m--output22m, 1m--noheadings22m, 1m--raw22m, and 1m--json22m.

     1m-O22m, 1m--output 4m22mcolumn24m[,4mcolumn24m]...
         Specify  the columns that are to be printed for the 1m--list 22moutput. Use 1m--help 22mto get a list
         of all supported columns.

     1m--output-all0m
         Output all available columns.

     1m-n22m, 1m--noheadings0m
         Don’t print headings for 1m--list 22moutput format.

     1m--raw0m
         Use the raw 1m--list 22moutput format.

     1m-J22m, 1m--json0m
         Use JSON format for 1m--list 22moutput.

     1m--remove 4m22mloopdev24m...
         Remove the specified loop device(s). The loop device must be unused  (not  associated  with
         any  backing  file).  This  option  removes the device node from the system. In most cases,
         1m--detach 22mis sufficient for normal use. See the 1mLOOP DEVICE LIFECYCLE 22msection below.

     1m-h22m, 1m--help0m
         Display help text and exit.

     1m-V22m, 1m--version0m
         Display version and exit.

1mLOOP DEVICE LIFECYCLE0m
     Loop devices go through several states during their lifecycle:

     1mCreation0m
         When 1mlosetup 22massociates a loop device with a backing file, it automatically creates the de‐
         vice node (e.g., 4m/dev/loop024m) if it doesn’t already exist. This happens on-demand  when  you
         use  options  like  1m-f 22mor specify a loop device explicitly. The device is created using the
         1mLOOP_CTL_ADD 22mioctl.

     1mDetachment0m
         The 1m-d 22m(1m--detach22m) option disassociates the backing file from  the  loop  device  using  the
         1mLOOP_CLR_FD 22mioctl. After detachment, the loop device node remains in 4m/dev24m and can be reused
         for another backing file. Use 1mlsblk -a 22mto see all loop device nodes, including unused ones.

     1mRemoval0m
         The  1m--remove  22moption  completely  removes  the  loop device node from the system using the
         1mLOOP_CTL_REMOVE 22mioctl. The device must be detached first (not associated with  any  backing
         file). After removal, the device node disappears from 4m/dev24m.

1mENCRYPTION0m
     1mCryptoloop is no longer supported in favor of dm-crypt. 22mFor more details see 1mcryptsetup22m(8).

1mEXIT STATUS0m
     1mlosetup  22mreturns  0  on success, nonzero on failure. When 1mlosetup 22mdisplays the status of a loop
     device, it returns 1 if the device is not configured and 2 if an error occurred which prevented
     determining the status of the device.

1mNOTES0m
     Since version 2.37 1mlosetup 22muses 1mLOOP_CONFIGURE 22mioctl to set up a new loop device by  one  ioctl
     call. The old versions use 1mLOOP_SET_FD 22mand 1mLOOP_SET_STATUS64 22mioctls to do the same.

1mENVIRONMENT0m
     1mLOOPDEV_DEBUG22m=all
         enables debug output.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_DEBUG22m=all
         enables libsmartcols debug output.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_DEBUG_PADDING22m=on
         use visible padding characters.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_JSON22m=compact|lines
         Controls JSON output format when using 1m--json22m. Supported values are 1mcompact 22mfor JSON output
         with minimal whitespace, and 1mlines 22mfor JSON Lines format (one JSON object per line). If un‐
         set or set to any other value, pretty-printed JSON is used.

1mFILES0m
     4m/dev/loop[0..N]0m
         loop block devices

     4m/dev/loop-control0m
         loop control device

1mEXAMPLE0m
     The following commands can be used as an example of using the loop device.

         # dd if=/dev/zero of=~/file.img bs=1024k count=10
         # losetup --find --show ~/file.img
         /dev/loop0
         # mkfs -t ext2 /dev/loop0
         # mount /dev/loop0 /mnt
         ...
         # umount /dev/loop0
         # losetup --detach /dev/loop0

1mAUTHORS0m
     34mKarel Zak 0m<kzak@redhat.com>, based on the original version from 34mTheodore Ts’o0m
     <tytso@athena.mit.edu>.

1mREPORTING BUGS0m
     For bug reports, use the 34missue tracker 0m<https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/issues>.

1mAVAILABILITY0m
     The 1mlosetup 22mcommand is part of the util-linux package which can be downloaded from 34mLinux Kernel0m
     34mArchive 0m<https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/utils/util-linux/>.

4mMSTARCHIVE24m(1)                               User Commands                              4mMSTARCHIVE24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     mstarchive - generate MFA2 archives

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     NAME

            mstarchive

     SYNOPSIS

            mstarchive OPTIONS

            [-h|--help]  [-v|--version  version]  [-o|--out-file  out_file] [-b|--bins-dir bins_dir]
            [-m|--mfa2-file mfa2_file]

     DESCRIPTION

            Allows the user to create a file with the MFA2 extension. The new file contains  several
            binary files of a given firmware for different adapter cards.

     OPTIONS

            mstarchive OPTIONS

     1m-h22m|--help
            : Show help message and exit

     1m-v22m|--version version
            : MFA2 version in the following format: x.x.x

     1m-o22m|--out-file out_file
            : Output file

     1m-b22m|--bins-dir bins_dir
            : Directory with the binaries files

     1m-m22m|--mfa2-file mfa2_file

1mNAME0m
     mstconfig - set or query non-volatile configurable options for Mellanox HCAs

1mDESCRIPTION0m
            NAME

            mstconfig

            SYNOPSIS

            mstconfig [Options] <Commands> [Parameters]

            DESCRIPTION:

            Allows the user to change some of the device configurations without having to create and
            burn a new firmware.

            OPTIONS:

     1m-d22m|--dev <device>
            Perform operation for a specified MST device.

     1m-b22m|--db <filename>
            Use a specific database file.

     1m-f22m|--file <conf_file>
            raw configuration file.

     1m-h22m|--help
            Display help message.

     1m-v22m|--version
            Display version info.

     1m-e22m|--enable_verbosity
            Show default and current configurations.

     1m-y22m|--yes
            Answer yes in prompt.

     1m-a22m|--all_attrs
            Show all attributes in the XML template

     1m-p22m|--private_key
            pem file for private key

     1m-u22m|--key_uuid
            keypair uuid

1mCOMMANDS0m
     clear_semaphore
            clear the tool semaphore.

     i[show_confs]
            display information about all configurations.

     q[uery]
            query supported configurations.

     r[eset]
            reset all configurations to their default value.

     s[et]  set configurations to a specific device.

     set_raw
            set raw configuration file.(only Connect-IB/Connect-X4/LX.)

     backup
            backup configurations to a file (only Connect-IB/Connect-X4/LX.). Use set_raw command to
            restore file.

     gen_tlvs_file
            Generate List of all TLVs. TLVs output file name must be specified. (*)

     g[en_xml_template]
            Generate  XML template. TLVs input file name and XML output file name must be specified.
            (*)

     xml2raw
            Generate Raw file from XML file. XML input file name and raw output file  name  must  be
            specified. (*)

     raw2xml
            Generate  XML  file  from Raw file. raw input file name and XML output file name must be
            specified. (*)

     xml2bin
            Generate Bin file from XML file. XML input file name and bin output file  name  must  be
            specified. (*)

     create_conf
            Generate  Configuration file from XML file. XML input file name and bin output file name
            must be specified. (*)

     apply  Apply a Configuration file. bin input file name must be specified. (*)

            (*) These commands do not require MST device

            To show supported configurations by device type, run show_confs command

            Examples:

     To query configurations
            mstconfig 1m-d 22m04:00.0 query

     To set configuration
            mstconfig 1m-d 22m04:00.0 set SRIOV_EN=1 NUM_OF_VFS=16 WOL_MAGIC_EN_P1=1

     To set raw configuration
            mstconfig 1m-d 22m05:00.0 1m-f 22mconf_file set_raw

     To reset configuration
            mstconfig 1m-d 22m04:00.0 reset

            Supported devices:

            4th Generation devices: ConnectX3, ConnectX3-Pro (FW 2.31.5000 and above).  5th  Genera‐
            tion devices: ConnectIB, ConnectX4, ConnectX4-LX, ConnectX5.

            Note: query device to view supported configurations by Firmware.

1mNAME0m
     mstflint - Flash Interface

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     NAME mstflint - Flash Interface

1mSYNOPSIS0m
            mstflint [OPTIONS] <command> [Parameters]

            [-d|--device  <device>]  [-i|--image  <image>]  [--latest_fw]  [--ir] [-h|--help] [--hh]
            [-y|--yes] [--no] [--guid <GUID>] [--guids <GUIDS...>] [--mac <MAC>] [--macs  <MACs...>]
            [--uid <UID>] [--blank_guids] [--clear_semaphore] [--qq] [--low_cpu] [--flashed_version]
            [--nofs]    [--allow_rom_change]    [--override_cache_replacement]   [--no_flash_verify]
            [--use_fw]   [-s|--silent]   [--vsd   <string>]   [--use_image_ps]   [--use_image_guids]
            [--use_image_rom]   [--use_dev_rom]  [--ignore_dev_data]  [--no_fw_ctrl]  [--dual_image]
            [--striped_image] [--banks <bank>] [--log <log_file>] [--flash_params  <type,  log2size,
            num_of_flashes>]  [-v|--version]  [--private_key  <key_file>]  [--key_uuid  <uuid_file>]
            [--private_key2 <key_file>] [--hmac_key <hmac_key>] [--key_uuid2 <uuid_file>]

     DESCRIPTION

            flint is a FW (firmware) burning and flash memory operations tool for  Mellanox  Infini‐
            band HCAs,Ethernet NIC cards, and switch devices.

1mOPTIONS0m
     1m-d22m|--device <device>
            Device flash is connected to.  Commands affected: all

     1m-i22m|--image <image>
            Binary image file.  Commands affected: burn, verify

     1m--latest_fw0m
            : Commands affected: burn

     1m--ir   22m: Commands affected: burn

     1m-h22m|--help
            Prints this message and exits

     1m--hh   22mPrints extended command help

     1m-y22m|--yes
            Non interactive mode - assume answer "yes" to all questions.  Commands affected: all

     1m--no   22mNon interactive mode - assume answer "no" to all questions.  Commands affected: all

     1m--guid 22m<GUID>
            GUID base value. 4 GUIDs are automatically assigned to the following values:

     guid   -> node GUID

     guid+1 -> port1
            guid+2 -> port2 guid+3 -> system image GUID.

     Note: port2 guid will be assigned even for a
            single port HCA - The HCA ignores this value.

            Commands affected: burn, sg

     1m--guids 22m<GUIDS...>
            4  GUIDs  must  be  specified  here.   The specified GUIDs are assigned to the following
            fields, respectively: node, port1, port2 and system image GUID.

     Note: port2 guid must be specified even for
            a single port HCA - The HCA ignores this value.  It can be set to 0x0.

            Commands affected: burn, sg

     1m--mac 22m<MAC>
            MAC address base value. 2 MACs are automatically assigned to the following values:

     mac    -> port1

     mac+1  -> port2

            Commands affected: burn, sg

     1m--macs 22m<MACs...>
            2 MACs must be specified here.  The specified MACs are assigned to port1, port2, respec‐
            tively.  Commands affected: burn, sg

     Note: 1m-mac22m/-macs flags are applicable only
            for Mellanox

            Technologies ethernet products.

     1m--uid 22m<UID>
            ConnectIB/SwitchIB only. Derive and set the device UIDs (GUIDs, MACs, WWNs).   UIDs  are
            derived  from  the  given  base UID according to Mellanox Methodology Commands affected:
            burn, sg

     1m--blank_guids0m
            Burn the image with blank GUIDs and MACs (where applicable). These  values  can  be  set
            later using the "sg" command (see details below).

            Commands affected: burn

     1m--clear_semaphore0m
            Force  clear the flash semaphore on the device.  No command is allowed when this flag is
            used.  NOTE: May result in system instability or flash corruption if the device  or  an‐
            other application is currently using the flash.  Exercise caution.

     1m--qq   22mRun  a  quick  query. When specified, flint will not perform full image integrity checks
            during the query operation. This may shorten execution time when running over  slow  in‐
            terfaces (e.g., I2C, MTUSB-1).  Commands affected: query

     1m--low_cpu0m
            :  When  specified, cpu usage will be reduced.  Run time might be increased Commands af‐
            fected: query

     1m--flashed_version0m
            : When specified, only flashed fw version is fetched Commands affected: query

     1m--nofs0m
            Burn image in a non failsafe manner.

     1m--allow_rom_change0m
            Allow burning/removing a ROM to/from FW image when product version is present.  Use only
            if you know what you are doing

     1m--override_cache_replacement0m
            On SwitchX/ConnectIB devices: Allow accessing the flash even if  the  cache  replacement
            mode  is enabled.  NOTE: This flag is intended for advanced users only.  Running in this
            mode may cause the firmware to hang.

     1m--no_flash_verify0m
            Do not verify each write on the flash.

     1m--use_fw0m
            Flash access will be done using FW (ConnectX-3/ConnectX-3Pro only).

     1m-s22m|--silent
            Do not print burn progress flyer.  Commands affected: burn

     1m--vsd 22m<string>
            Write this string, of up to 208 characters, to VSD when burn.

     1m--use_image_ps0m
            Burn vsd as appears in the given image - do not keep existing VSD  on  flash.   Commands
            affected: burn

     1m--use_image_guids0m
            Burn (guids/macs) as appears in the given image.  Commands affected: burn

     1m--use_image_rom0m
            Do not save the ROM which exists in the device.  Commands affected: burn

     1m--use_dev_rom0m
            Save the ROM which exists in the device.  Commands affected: burn

     1m--ignore_dev_data0m
            Do  not attempt to take device data sections from device(sections will be taken from the
            image. FS3 Only).  Commands affected: burn

     1m--no_fw_ctrl0m
            Do not attempt to work with the FW Ctrl update commands

     1m--dual_image0m
            Make the burn process burn two images on flash (previously default algorithm).   Current
            default failsafe burn process burns a single image (in alternating locations).  Commands
            affected: burn

     1m--striped_image0m
            Use  this  flag  to  indicate  that the given image file is in a "striped image" format.
            Commands affected: query verify

     1m--banks 22m<bank>
            Set the number of attached flash devices (banks)

     1m--log 22m<log_file>
            Print the burning status to the specified log file

     1m--flash_params 22m<type, log2size,

     num_of_flashes>
            Use the given parameters to access the flash

     instead of reading them from the flash.
            Supported parameters: Type: The type of the flash,  such  as:M25PXxx,  M25Pxx,  N25Q0XX,
            SST25VFxx,   W25QxxBV,   W25Xxx,  W25Qxxx,  W25Qxxx,  AT25DFxxx,  S25FLXXXP,  S25FL11xx,
            MX25L16xxx,  MX25Lxxx,  S25FLxxx,  IS25LPxxx.   log2size:  The   log2   of   the   flash
            size.num_of_flashes: the number of the flashes connected to the device.

     1m-v22m|--version
            Version info.

     1m--private_key 22m<key_file>
            path to PEM formatted private key to be used by the sign command

     1m--key_uuid 22m<uuid_file>
            UUID matching the given private key to be used by the sign command

     1m--private_key2 22m<key_file>
            path to PEM formatted private key to be used by the sign command

     1m--hmac_key 22m<hmac_key>
            path to file containing key (For FS4 image only).

     1m--key_uuid2 22m<uuid_file>
            UUID matching the given private key to be used by the sign command

     COMMANDS SUMMARY

     burn|b 1m-ir0m
            Burn flash. Use "-ir burn" flag to perform

            image reactivation prior burning.

     query|q [full]
            Query misc. flash/firmware characteristics,

            use "full" to get more information.

     verify|v [showitoc]
            Verify entire flash, use "showitoc" to see

            ITOC headers in FS3/FS4 image only.

     swreset
            SW reset the target switch device.This

            command is supported only in the In-Band access method.

     brom   <ROM-file>                            : Burn the specified ROM file on the flash.

     drom   Remove the ROM section from the flash.

     rrom   <out-file>                            : Read the ROM section from the flash.

     bb     Burn Block - Burns the given image as is. No

            checks are done.

     sg     [guids_num=<num|num_port1,num_port2>

            step_size=<size|size_port1,size_port2>] | [nocrc]                                      :
            Set GUIDs.  sv                                           : Set the VSD.  ri   <out-file>
            :  Read  the fw image on the flash.  dc   [out-file]                              : Dump
            Configuration: print fw configuration

            file for the given image.

     dh     [out-file]                              : Dump Hash: dump the hash if it is integrated

            in the FW image

     set_key
            [key]                              : Set/Update the HW access key which is used to

     enable/disable access to HW.
            The key can be provided in the command line or interactively typed after the command  is
            given NOTE: The new key is activated only after the device is reset.

     hw_access
            <enable|disable> [key]           : Enable/disable the access to the HW.

     The key can be provided in the command line
            or interactively typed after the command is given

     hw     query                                   : Query HW info and flash attributes.

     erase|e <addr>
            Erases sector.

     rw     <addr>                                  : Read one dword from flash

     ww     <addr> <data>                           : Write one dword to flash

     wwne   <addr> <data>                         : Write one dword to flash without sector

            erase

     wbne   <addr> <size> <data ...>              : Write a data block to flash without sector

            erase.

     wb     <data-file> <addr>                      : Write a data block to flash.

     rb     <addr> <size> [out-file]                : Read  a data block from flash

     clear_semaphore
            Clear flash semaphore.

     qrom   query ROM image.

     checksum|cs
            perform MD5 checksum on FW.

            timestamp|ts          <set|query|reset>         [timestamp]         [FW         version]
            : FW time stamping.  cache_image|ci                               : cache FW  image(Win‐
            dows  only).   sign                                          :  Sign firmware image file
            sign_with_hmac                               :  Sign  image  with  HMAC  set_public_keys
            [public  keys  binary  file]   :  Set Public Keys (For FS3/FS4 image only).  set_forbid‐
            den_versions   [forbidden versions binary  file]                                  :  Set
            Forbidden Versions (For FS3/FS4 image

            only).

     image_reactivate|ir
            : Reactivate previous flash image. For FW

            controlled devices only.

     binary_compare|bc
            : Binary compare between device firmware and

            given BIN file. If there is a silent mode, no progress is displayed.

1mRETURN VALUES0m
     0      Successful completion.

     1      An error has occurred.

     7      For burn command - FW already updated - burn was aborted.

1mSEE ALSO0m

1mNAME0m
     mstfwmanager - Mellanox Firmware Manager

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     NAME

            mstfwmanager

     SYNOPSIS

            mstfwmanager

            [-d|--dev  DeviceName]  [-h|--help]  [-v|--version]  [--query]  [--query-format  Format]
            [-u|--update] [-i|--image-file  FileName]  [-D|--image-dir  DirectoryName]  [-f|--force]
            [--no_fw_ctrl]  [-y|--yes]  [--no]  [--clear-semaphore] [--exe-rel-path] [-l|--list-con‐
            tent] [--archive-names] [--nofs]  [--log]  [-L|--log-file  LogFileName]  [--no-progress]
            [-o|--outfile   OutputFileName]   [--online]  [--online-query-psid  PSIDs]  [--key  key]
            [--download DirectoryName] [--download-default] [--get-download-opt OPT] [--download-de‐
            vice Device] [--download-os OS] [--download-type Type] [--ssl-certificate Certificate]

     DESCRIPTION

            Mellanox Firmware Manager

     OPTIONS

            mstfwmanager

     1m-d22m|--dev DeviceName
            : Perform operation for specified mst device(s). Run 'mst status' command  to  list  the
            available  devices.  Multiple devices can be specified delimited by semicolons. A device
            list containing semicolons must be quoted.

     1m-h22m|--help
            : Show this message and exit

     1m-v22m|--version
            : Show the executable version and exit

     1m--query0m
            : Query device(s) info

     1m--query-format 22mFormat
            : (Query | Online query) output format, XML | Text - default Text

     1m-u22m|--update
            : Update firmware image(s) on the device(s)

     1m-i22m|--image-file FileName
            : Specified image file to use

     1m-D22m|--image-dir DirectoryName
            : Specified directory instead of default to locate image files

     1m-f22m|--force
            : Force image update

     1m--no_fw_ctrl0m
            : Don't use FW Ctrl update

     1m-y22m|--yes
            : Answer is yes in prompts

     1m--no   22m: Answer is no in prompts

     1m--clear-semaphore0m
            : Force clear the flash semaphore on the device, No command is allowed when this flag is
            used. NOTE: May result in system instability or flash corruption if the  device  or  an‐
            other application is currently using the flash. Exercise caution.

     1m--exe-rel-path0m
            : Use paths relative to the location of the executable

     1m-l22m|--list-content
            : List file/Directory content, used with 1m--image-dir 22mand 1m--image-file 22mflags

     1m--archive-names0m
            : Display archive names in listing

     1m--nofs0m
            : Burn image in a non failsafe manner

     1m--log  22m: Create log file

     1m-L22m|--log-file LogFileName
            : Use specified log file

     1m--no-progress0m
            : Do not show progress

     1m-o22m|--outfile OutputFileName
            : Write to specified output file

     1m--online0m
            : Fetch required FW images online from Mellanox server

     1m--online-query-psid 22mPSIDs
            : Query FW info, PSID(s) are comma separated

     1m--key 22mkey
            : Key for custom download/update

     1m--download 22mDirectoryName
            : Download files from server to a specified directory

     1m--download-default0m
            : Use Default values for download

     1m--get-download-opt 22mOPT
            : Get download options for OS or Device Options are: OS, Device

     1m--download-device 22mDevice
            :  Use  '--get-download-opt Device' option to view available devices for device specific
            downloads

     1m--download-os 22mOS
            : Only for self_extractor download: Use '--get-download-opt OS' option to view available
            OS for sfx download

     1m--download-type 22mType
            : MFA | self_extractor - default All

     1m--ssl-certificate 22mCertificate
            : SSL certificate For secure connection

1mEXAMPLES0m
            1. Query specific device or all devices (if no device were supplied) >> mstfwmanager [-d
            <device>] [--query] 2. Burn device with specific image / MFA / images directory >>  mst‐
            fwmanager  -d <device> [-i <image file/MFA file> | -D <images dir>] 3. Update the card's
            firmware >> mstfwmanager -u 4. Update the card's firmware from latest version on the web
            >> mstfwmanager --online -u 5. Download latest FW package from the web  >>  mstfwmanager
            --download-default --download-os Linux_x64 --download-type self_extractor

1mNAME0m
     mstfwreset - Query and perform reset operation on the device

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     usage: mstfwreset 1m--device 22mDEVICE [--level {0,3,4,5}] [--type {0,1}] [--yes]

            {q,query,r,reset,reset_fsm_register}

   1mmstfwreset : The tool provides the following functionality in order to load new firmware:0m
            1. Query the device for the supported reset-level and reset-type 2. Perform reset opera‐
            tion on the device

1mOPTIONS0m
     1m--device 22mDEVICE, 1m-d 22mDEVICE
            Device to work with

     1m--level 22m{0,3,4,5}, 1m-l 22m{0,3,4,5}

     1m--yes22m, 1m-y0m

     1m--skip_driver22m, 1m-s0m
            Skip driver start/stop stage (driver must be stopped manually)

     1m--mst_flags 22mMST_FLAGS, 1m-m 22mMST_FLAGS

            1m--mst_flags=22m"--with_fpga"

     1m--help22m, 1m-h0m

            ister.

     mstfwtrace - Extracts and prints trace messages generated by the firmware of 5th generation de‐
     vices

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     usage: mstfwtrace 1m-d22m|--device DEVICE [options]

   1moptional arguments:0m
     1m-h22m, 1m--help0m
            show this help message and exit

     1m-v22m, 1m--version22m, 1m-v0m
            Print tool version.

1mOPTIONS0m
     1m-d 22mDEVICE, 1m--device 22mDEVICE

     1m--tracer_mode 22mTRACER_MODE

     1m--real_ts0m

   1mFormat:0m

4mMSTLINK24m(1)                                  User Commands                                 4mMSTLINK24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     mstlink - check and debug link status and issues related to them

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     mstlink [OPTIONS]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     The  mlxlink  tool is used to check and debug link status and issues related to them.  The tool
     can be used on different links and cables (passive, active, transceiver and backplane).

1mOPTIONS0m
     1m-h 22m|--help
            : Display help message.

     1m-v 22m|--version
            : Display version info.

     1m-d 22m|--device
            <device>               : Perform operation for a specified mst device

     1m-p 22m|--port
            <port_number_or_list>  : Port Number, or a comma-separated list of ports (e.g. 1,2,3). A
            list is currently supported only with 1m-a22m/--port_state.

     1m--port_type0m
            <port_type>            : Port Type [NETWORK(Default)/PCIE]

     1m--depth0m
            <depth>                : depth level of the DUT of some hierarchy (PCIE only)

     1m--pcie_index0m
            <pcie_index>           : PCIe index number (Internal domain index) (PCIE only)

     1m--node0m
            <node>                 : the node within each depth (PCIE only)

     1m--json0m
            : Print the output in json format

            QUERIES:

     1m--show_links0m
            : Show valid PCIe links (PCIE only)

     1m-m 22m|--show_module
            : Show Module Info. When  combined  with  --cable,  shows  the  module  pre-coding  info
            (Host/Line Tx/Rx operational status)

     1m-c 22m|--show_counters
            : Show Physical Counters and BER Info

     1m-e 22m|--show_eye
            : Show Eye Opening Info

     1m--show_fec0m
            : Show FEC Capabilities

     1m--show_serdes_tx0m
            : Show Transmitter Info

     1m--show_device0m
            : General Device Info

     1m--show_ber_monitor0m
            : Show BER Monitor Info (not supported for HCA)

     1m--show_external_phy0m
            : Show External PHY Info

            COMMANDS:

     1m-a 22m|--port_state <port_state>
            : Configure Port State [UP(up)/DN(down)/TG(toggle)]

     1m-s 22m|--speeds
            <speeds>               : Configure Speeds [speed1,speed2,...]

     1m--link_mode_force0m
            : Configure Link Mode Force (Disable AN)

     1m-l 22m|--loopback
            <loopback>               :   Configure   Loopback  Mode  [NO(no  loopback)/PH(phy  loop‐
            back)/EX(external loopback)]

     1m-k 22m|--fec
            <fec_override>                   :   Configure   FEC    [AU(Auto)/NF(No-FEC)/FC(FireCode
            FEC)/RS(RS-FEC)]

     1m--fec_speed0m
            <fec_speed>                 :  Speed to Configure FEC [100G/50G/25G/...] (Default is Ac‐
            tive Speed)

     1m--serdes_tx0m
            <params>               : Configure Transmitter Parameters [polarity,ob_tap0,...]

     1m--serdes_tx_lane 22m<transmitter_lane>
            : Transmitter Lane to Set (Optional - Default All Lanes)

     1m--database0m
            : Save Transmitter Configuration for Current Speed Permanently (Optional)

     1m--test_mode0m
            <prbs_mode>             :   Physical   Test   Mode   Configuration   [EN(enable)/DS(dis‐
            able)/TU(perform tuning)]

     1m--rx_prbs0m
            <rx_prbs_mode>              :  RX  PRBS Mode [PRBS31(Default)/PRBS7/...] (Optional - De‐
            fault PRBS31)

     1m--tx_prbs0m
            <tx_prbs_mode>             : TX PRBS Mode [PRBS31(Default)/PRBS7/...]  (Optional  -  De‐
            fault PRBS31)

     1m--rx_rate0m
            <rx_lane_rate>              :  RX  Lane Rate [EDR(Default)/25G/10G/...]  (Optional - De‐
            fault 25G)

     1m--tx_rate0m
            <tx_lane_rate>             : TX Lane Rate [EDR(Default)/25G/10G/...]   (Optional  -  De‐
            fault 25G)

     1m-b 22m|--ber_collect <csv_file>
            : Port Extended Information Collection [CSV File]

     1m--ber_limit0m
            <limit_criteria>            :  BER  Limit  Criteria [Nominal(Default)/Corner/Drift] (Op‐
            tional - Default Nominal)

     1m--iteration0m
            <iteration>                : Iteration Number of BER Collection

     1m--pc   22m: Clear Counters

     1m--set_external_phy0m
            : Set External PHY (not supported for HCA)

     1m--twisted_pair_force_mode 22m<twisted_pair_force_mode>
            : Twisted Pair Force Mode [MA(Master)/SL(Slave)]

1mEXAMPLES0m
     get info of <device>, <port_number>
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number>

            get info of <device>, <port_number> and BER Counters:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m-c0m

            get info of <device>, <port_number> and Transmitter Parameters:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--show_serdes_tx0m

     Configure Port State
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--port_state 22mUP

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m1,2,3 1m--port_state 22mDN

     Configure Port Speeds
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--speeds 22m25G,50G,100G

     Configure FEC
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--fec 22mRS

     Configure Port for Physical Test Mode
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--test_mode  22mEN  (1m--rx_prbs  22mPRBS31  1m--rx_rate  22m25G
            1m--tx_prbs 22mPRBS7 1m--tx_rate 22m10G)

     Perform PRBS Tuning
            :

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> 1m--test_mode 22mTU

            Configure Transmitter Parameters (on lane, to database):

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m-p 22m<port_number> (1m--serdes_tx_lane 22m<lane number>) (1m--database22m) \
              1m--serdes_tx 22m<polarity>,<ob_tap0>,<ob_tap1>,<ob_tap2>,<ob_bias>,<ob_preemp_mode>

     PCIe queries (supported on HCA, CPU and Switches that advertise PCIe management):
            :

            List valid PCIe links:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--port_type 22mPCIE 1m--show_links0m

            Show PCIe operational info for a specific link:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--port_type 22mPCIE 1m--depth 22m<d> 1m--pcie_index 22m<i> 1m--node 22m<n>

            Show PCIe BER/MPCNT counters:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--port_type 22mPCIE 1m-c0m

            Collect amBER for PCIe links:

            mstlink 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--port_type 22mPCIE 1m--amber_collect 22m<file.csv>

            Note: 1m--pcie_error_injection 22mis supported on HCA devices only.

1mSEE ALSO0m

4mMSTMCRA24m(1)                                  User Commands                                 4mMSTMCRA24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     mstmcra - Mellanox Configuration Registers Access tool

1mDESCRIPTION0m
            Mellanox  Configuration  Registers  Access tool Usage: mstmcra [-s <i2c-slave>] [-a <adb
            dump>] [-v] [-h] [-c] <device>

            <addr[.<bit offset>:<bit size>]|[,<bytes number>]> [data] If data is given, operation is
            write. Otherwise  it  is  read.   If  a  bit  range  is  given  in  the  address  (E.G.:
            0xf0014.16:8):

     For read
            - Only the requested bits are printed.

            For write - Read-Modify-Write. Only the requested bits are changed.

            If 'bytes number' is given in the address (E.G.: 0xf0014,16):

     For read
            - Will read a block (its size is the given bytes number).

            For write - User need to give list of dwrods to write,

            number of dwords should be (bytes number/4).

     DESCRIPTION:

            Reads/writes a single word from/to a device configuration register space

     1m-s 22m<i2c-slave> : I2C slave address.

     1m-a 22m<dump file> : adb dump file, used for access by path.

     1m-c     22m: clear the device's PCI semaphore.

     1m-h     22m: Print this help message.

     1m-v     22m: Display version info

   1mEnvironment Variables:0m
     ADB_DUMP
            : Holds the path to adb dump, used for access by path (can be overridden by "-a").

1mNAME0m

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     usage: mstprivhost [-h] [-v] 1m--device 22mDEVICE [--disable_rshim]

            [--disable_tracer]  [--disable_counter_rd]  [--disable_port_owner]  {r,restrict,p,privi‐
            lege}

     restrict or privilege host Note: New configurations takes effect immediately.  Note: privileged
     host - host has all supported privileges.

            restricted host - host is not allowed to modify global  per  port/parameters  or  access
            other hosts parametersis.

   1moptional arguments:0m
     1m-h22m, 1m--help0m
            show this help message and exit

     1m-v22m, 1m--version0m
            show program's version number and exit

1mOPTIONS0m
     1m--device 22mDEVICE, 1m-d 22mDEVICE
            Device to work with.

     1m--disable_rshim0m
            When TRUE, the host does not have an RSHIM function to access the embedded CPU registers
            mlxconfig_name: HOST_DISABLE_RSHIM

     1m--disable_tracer0m
            When  TRUE,  the  host  will  not be allowed to own the Tracer mlxconfig_name: HOST_DIS‐
            ABLE_TRACER_OWNER

     1m--disable_counter_rd0m
            When TRUE, the host will not be allowed to read Physical port  counters  mlxconfig_name:

     1m--disable_port_owner0m

            ABLE_PORT_OWNER

   1mCommands:0m

1mNAME0m
     mstreg - Expose supported access registers

1mDESCRIPTION0m
            NAME:

            mstreg

            SYNOPSIS:

            mstreg [OPTIONS]

            DESCRIPTION:

            Exposes supported access registers, and allows users to obtain information regarding the
            registers fields and attributes, and to set and get data with specific register.

            OPTIONS:

     1m-h 22m|--help
            : Display help message.

     1m-v 22m|--version
            : Display version info.

     1m-d 22m|--device
            <device>               : Perform operation for a specified mst device.

     1m-a 22m|--adb_file
            <adb_file>             : An external ADB file

     1m--reg_name0m
            <reg_name>             : Known access register name

     1m--reg_id0m
            <reg_ID>               : Access register ID

     1m--reg_len0m
            <reg_length>           : Access register layout length (bytes)

     1m-i 22m|--indexes
            <idxs_vals>            : Register indexes

     1m-g 22m|--get
            : Register access GET

     1m-s 22m|--set
            <reg_dataStr>          : Register access SET

     1m--show_reg0m
            <reg_name>             : Print the fields of a given reg access (must have reg_name)

     1m--show_regs0m
            : Print all available reg access'

     1m--yes  22m: Non-interactive mode, answer yes to all questions

            Examples:

     Show all available access register
            : mstreg 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--show_regs0m

     Show all fields of register PAOS
            : mstreg 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--show_reg 22mPAOS

            GET PAOS with indexes: local port 0x1 and swid 0x5:

            mstreg 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--get --reg_name 22mPAOS 1m--indexes 22m"local_port=0x1,swid=0x5"

            SET PAOS with indexes: local port 0x1 and swid 0x5, and data: e 0x0:

            mstreg 1m-d 22m<device> 1m--set 22m"e=0x0" 1m--reg_name 22mPAOS 1m--indexes 22m"local_port=0x1,swid=0x5"

1mNAME0m
     mv - move (rename) files

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     1mmv 22m[4mOPTION24m]... [4m-T24m] 4mSOURCE24m 4mDEST0m
     1mmv 22m[4mOPTION24m]... 4mSOURCE24m... 4mDIRECTORY0m
     1mmv 22m[4mOPTION24m]... 4m-t24m 4mDIRECTORY24m 4mSOURCE24m...

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Rename SOURCE to DEST, or move SOURCE(s) to DIRECTORY.

     Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--backup1m--backup[=CONTROL]22m8;;
            make a backup of each existing destination file

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-b1m-b22m8;;     like 1m--backup 22mbut does not accept an argument

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--debug1m--debug22m8;;
            explain how a file is copied.  Implies 1m-v0m

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--exchange1m--exchange22m8;;
            exchange source and destination

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-f1m-f, --force22m8;;
            do not prompt before overwriting

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-i1m-i, --interactive22m8;;
            prompt before overwrite

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-n1m-n, --no-clobber22m8;;
            (deprecated) silently skip existing files.  See also 1m--update0m

     If you specify more than one of 1m-i22m, 1m-f22m, 1m-n22m, only the final one takes effect.

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--no-copy1m--no-copy22m8;;
            do not copy if renaming fails

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--strip-trailing-slashes1m--strip-trailing-slashes22m8;;
            remove any trailing slashes from each SOURCE argument

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-S1m-S, --suffix=SUFFIX22m8;;
            override the usual backup suffix

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-t1m-t, --target-directory=DIRECTORY22m8;;
            move all SOURCE arguments into DIRECTORY

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-T1m-T, --no-target-directory22m8;;
            treat DEST as a normal file

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv--update1m--update[=UPDATE]22m8;;
            control which existing files are updated; UPDATE={all,none,none-fail,older(default)}

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-u1m-u22m8;;     equivalent to 1m--update22m[=4molder24m].  See below

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-v1m-v, --verbose22m8;;
            explain what is being done

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#mv-Z1m-Z, --context22m8;;
            set SELinux security context of destination file to default type

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/mv#mv--help1m--help22m8;;
            display this help and exit

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/mv#mv--version1m--version22m8;;
            output version information and exit

     UPDATE controls which existing files in the destination are replaced.  'all' is the default op‐
     eration when an 1m--update 22moption is not specified, and results in all existing files in the des‐
     tination  being replaced.  'none' is like the 1m--no-clobber 22moption, in that no files in the des‐
     tination are replaced, and skipped files do not induce a failure.  'none-fail' also ensures  no
     files  are  replaced in the destination, but any skipped files are diagnosed and induce a fail‐
     ure.  'older' is the default operation when 1m--update 22mis specified, and results in  files  being
     replaced if they're older than the corresponding source file.

     The  backup  suffix is '~', unless set with 1m--suffix 22mor SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX.  The version con‐
     trol method may be selected via the 1m--backup 22moption or through the VERSION_CONTROL  environment
     variable.  Here are the values:

     none, off       never make backups (even if 1m--backup 22mis given)
     numbered, t     make numbered backups
     existing, nil   numbered if numbered backups exist, simple otherwise
     simple, never   always make simple backups

nvme-config-convert.text:
4mNVME-CONFIG-CONVER24m(1)                        NVMe Manual                       4mNVME-CONFIG-CONVER24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     nvme-config-convert - Convert a legacy NVMe-oF configuration to the INI format

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mconfig24m 4mconvert0m
                             [--config=<file> | -J <file>]
                             [--output=<file>]
                             [--force]
                             [--verbose | -v]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Converts a pre-3.0 NVMe-oF configuration from the legacy 4mconfig.json24m JSON store and/or the 4mdis‐0m
     4mcovery.conf24m  argv-style  file to the INI configuration format used by 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m and 4mnvme0m
     4mdiscover24m. The INI  format  is  documented  at  34m1mhttps://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/blob/mas‐0m
     1m34mter/libnvme/design/CONFIG.md0m

     By default, the command looks for the legacy files /usr/local/etc/nvme/config.json and /usr/lo‐
     cal/etc/nvme/discovery.conf  and  converts any that exist into a single configuration, matching
     the behavior of 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m. Use --config to convert a config.json at a  non-default  path
     instead;  as  with  4mnvme24m  4mconnect-all24m,  discovery.conf  conversion  is not gated by --config ——
     /usr/local/etc/nvme/discovery.conf is always converted when it exists, whether or not  --config
     is given.

     The  converted  configuration  is written to the file specified by --output. If --output is not
     specified, the default location, /usr/local/etc/nvme/nvme-fabrics.conf, is used. Unless --force
     is specified, the command refuses to overwrite an existing configuration. On success, the  con‐
     verted legacy file(s) are renamed to 4m<name>.converted24m to prevent conversion on subsequent runs.
     Running  the  command again is safe: a source file that is missing only because a prior run al‐
     ready converted and renamed it is treated as already done, not as an error.

     Malformed entries (for example, invalid addressing or an unreadable port) are  skipped  with  a
     log message. Conversion continues unless a memory allocation failure occurs.

1mOPTIONS0m
     -J <file>, --config=<file>
         Convert this JSON file instead of the default /usr/local/etc/nvme/config.json.

     --output=<file>
         Write the converted configuration here instead of the default /usr/local/etc/nvme/nvme-fab‐
         rics.conf.

     --force
         Overwrite an existing configuration at the target. Any manual changes are lost.

     -v, --verbose
         Increase the level of detail in the output.

1mEXAMPLES0m
     •   Convert the system’s legacy configuration in place:

             # nvme config convert

     •   Convert one specific configuration file for testing, without touching the system configura‐
         tion:

             # nvme config convert --config /tmp/config.json --output /tmp/nvme-fabrics.conf

         Note:  unlike config.json, discovery.conf has no --config-style override —— its path is al‐
         ways /usr/local/etc/nvme/discovery.conf. If that file exists on the  system,  this  command
         still  converts  it and renames it to 4mdiscovery.conf.converted24m, even though --config points
         elsewhere.

1mSEE ALSO0m

     cover(1) 34m1mhttps://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/blob/master/libnvme/design/CONFIG.md0m

1mNVME0m

nvme-config-create.text:
4mNVME-CONFIG-CREATE24m(1)                        NVMe Manual                       4mNVME-CONFIG-CREATE24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     nvme-config-create - Add an NVMe-oF connection entry to the INI configuration

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mconfig24m 4mcreate0m
                             [--discovery]
                             [--persistent[=<no|auto|force>] ]
                             [--host-symname=<name>]
                             [--output=<file>]
                             [<fabrics-options>]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Build  one  NVMe-oF connection entry from command-line options and add it to the INI configura‐
     tion used by 4mnvme24m 4mconnect24m, 4mnvme24m 4mdiscover24m, and 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m. The  format  is  documented  at
     34m1mhttps://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/blob/master/libnvme/design/CONFIG.md0m

     If  the  target  file exists, its connections are kept and the new entry is merged in alongside
     them. Running the same command again is a no-op. Unlike 4mnvme24m 4mconfig24m  4mconvert24m,  this  is  not  a
     one-shot migration; it is the ongoing way to build an INI configuration from the command line.

     The  entry is an I/O controller (subsystem) entry by default, and --nqn is required. Use --dis‐
     covery for a discovery controller entry instead; --nqn is then optional.

     A connection with an explicit --hostnqn or --hostid is written to a  drop-in  under  4m<file>.d/24m.
     One without either goes into the main file.

1mOPTIONS0m
     --discovery
         Create a discovery controller entry instead of an I/O controller entry. Without this, --nqn
         is required.

     --persistent[=<no|auto|force>]
         Record  this  discovery  controller’s  persistence  mode. Requires --discovery. Because the
         value is optional, it must be attached directly to the option (--persistent=force). A value
         given as a separate argument (--persistent force) is no value of the option  but  an  extra
         argument, and the command fails.

         •   4mauto24m  (the  default for every --discovery entry, whether or not --persistent is given):
             persist the connection only where the target’s own EPCSD (Explicit  Persistent  Connec‐
             tion Support for Discovery) flag reports support for it.

         •   4mforce24m: persist regardless of what EPCSD reports, for a target whose self-reported EPCSD
             cannot be trusted.

         •   4mno24m:  explicitly record that this discovery controller is not persistent, overriding any
             default that would otherwise apply.

     --host-symname=<name>
         Name this host persona. Puts it in its own configuration drop-in.

     --output=<file>
         Write to this file instead of the default /usr/local/etc/nvme/nvme-fabrics.conf.

1mFABRICS OPTIONS0m
     The following options are common to NVMe over Fabrics commands such as nvme connect:

     -a <traddr>, --traddr=<traddr>
         Specify the network address of the controller. For transports  using  IP  addressing  (e.g.
         rdma, tcp), this should be an IP address.

     --concat
         Enable secure concatenation (TCP).

     -c <#>, --reconnect-delay=<#>
         Set the delay in seconds before reconnect is attempted after a connection loss.

     -C <secret>, --kxchap-ctrl-secret=<secret>
         Controller  authentication  secret  for  bi-directional  authentication.  If not specified,
         bi-directional authentication is not attempted.

     -S <secret>, --kxchap-secret=<secret>
         Host authentication secret (KX-HMAC-CHAP). Must be provided in ASCII format as  defined  in
         the NVMe specification.

     -C <secret>, --dhchap-ctrl-secret=<secret>
         Controller  authentication  secret  for  bi-directional  authentication.  If not specified,
         bi-directional authentication is not attempted. (deprecated, see --kxchap-ctrl-secret)

     -S <secret>, --dhchap-secret=<secret>
         Host authentication secret (DH-HMAC-CHAP). Must be provided in ASCII format as  defined  in
         the NVMe specification. (deprecated, see --kxchap-secret)

     --disable-sqflow
         Disable submission queue flow control.

     -G, --data-digest
         Enable data digest generation/verification (TCP).

     -D, --duplicate-connect
         Allow duplicate connections to the same subsystem.

     -g, --hdr-digest
         Enable header digest generation/verification (TCP).

     -f <iface>, --host-iface=<iface>
         Specify the network interface to use for the connection.

     -I <hostid>, --hostid=<hostid>
         Specify the host UUID.

     -q <hostnqn>, --hostnqn=<hostnqn>
         Override the default host NQN.

     -w <traddr>, --host-traddr=<traddr>
         Specify the source address on the host side of the connection.

     -k <#>, --keep-alive-tmo=<#>
         Set the keep-alive timeout in seconds.

     --keyring=<keyring>
         Keyring to use for TLS key lookup.

     -n <subnqn>, --nqn=<subnqn>
         Specify the NVMe subsystem NQN to connect to.

     -i <#>, --nr-io-queues=<#>
         Number of I/O queues to create.

     -P <#>, --nr-poll-queues=<#>
         Number of polling queues to create.

     -W <#>, --nr-write-queues=<#>
         Number of write queues to create.

     -Q <#>, --queue-size=<#>
         Queue depth for I/O queues.

     -l <#>, --ctrl-loss-tmo=<#>
         Maximum time in seconds to retry reconnect attempts after controller loss.

     -s <trsvcid>, --trsvcid=<trsvcid>
         Transport service identifier (e.g. TCP/rdma port). Default is 4420 for RDMA.

     -T <#>, --tos=<#>
         Type of service value for the connection (TCP).

     -t <trtype>, --transport=<trtype>
         Specify the transport type. Supported values include:

     + allbox tab(:); lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt.  T{

     Value T}:T{

     Description T} T{

     rdma T}:T{

     RDMA (RoCE, iWARP, InfiniBand) T} T{

     tcp T}:T{

     TCP/IP T} T{

     fc T}:T{

     Fibre Channel (1mexperimental22m) T} T{

     loop T}:T{

     Local loopback transport T}


     --tls
         Enable TLS encryption (TCP).

     --tls-key=<tls-key>
         TLS  key  for the connection. It is recommended to preload keys into the system keyring in‐
         stead of passing them via the command line.

     --tls-key-identity=<identity>
         Identity associated with the TLS key.

1mGLOBAL OPTIONS0m
     The following options are defined at the top-level nvme command and are available to this  sub‐
     command:

     --dry-run
         Print the command that would be executed, but do not actually execute it.

     --no-ioctl-probing
         Disable probing for 64-bit IOCTL support.

     --no-retries
         Disable retry logic on transient errors.

     -o <fmt>, --output-format=<fmt>
         Set  the  reporting format to 4mnormal24m, 4mtabular,24m 4m'json24m, or 4mbinary24m. Only one output format may
         be used at a time.

1mNAME0m
     nvme-config-show - Show the resolved NVMe-oF INI connection configuration

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mconfig24m 4mshow0m
                             [--config=<file> | -J <file>]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Reads the NVMe-oF INI connection configuration file used by 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m and 4mnvme24m 4mdiscover24m,
     and   prints   every   configured   connection   entry.   The   INI  format  is  documented  at
     34m1mhttps://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/blob/master/libnvme/design/CONFIG.md0m

     By default, the file at /usr/local/etc/nvme/nvme-fabrics.conf is read. Use --config to  show  a
     file at a different path instead.

     In  the  default  and  4mtabular24m output formats, each entry is rendered as the equivalent command
     line that would establish it: 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m for a Discovery Controller entry,  4mnvme24m  4mconnect0m
     for  an  I/O Controller entry, preceded by a comment naming the entry’s source (which file/sec‐
     tion it came from). The 4mjson24m output format instead reports  each  entry’s  fields  individually
     (transport, address, NQN, host identity, and any extra connect parameters).

     hostname resolution attempted. A persona with no 4mhostnqn24m/4mhostid24m  set  is  shown  without  those
     fields rather than the system default it would resolve to at connect time, since showing a con‐
     crete value here would suggest a fixed identity the configuration doesn’t actually pin.

4mNVME-CONFIG-STATUS24m(1)                        NVMe Manual                       4mNVME-CONFIG-STATUS24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     nvme-config-status - Report legacy NVMe-oF config.json/discovery.conf conversion status

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mconfig24m 4mstatus0m

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Reports  the  on-disk state of the legacy pre-3.0 configuration files, /usr/local/etc/nvme/con‐
     fig.json and /usr/local/etc/nvme/discovery.conf, and of the 4m*.converted24m marker 4mnvme24m 4mconfig24m 4mcon‐0m
     4mvert24m leaves next to each one it converts. This command never modifies or converts anything;  it
     only reports state.

     One line is printed for each legacy file that has something to report:

     •   4mpresent,24m 4mnot24m 4myet24m 4mconverted24m —— the file exists and has never been converted.

     •   4mpresent,24m  4malready24m  4mconverted24m  ——  the  file exists and a 4m<file>.converted24m marker (a symlink
         pointing back at the file itself, left in place deliberately so a rollback to a pre-INI in‐
         stallation still finds the original legacy file) confirms it was converted. Both  the  file
         and the marker can be deleted once rollback is no longer a concern.

     •   4mnot24m  4mpresent24m 4m(a24m 4mstale24m 4mmarker24m 4mexists)24m —— the file is gone but its 4m<file>.converted24m marker is
         still there, dangling. This is left over from an earlier conversion and is always  safe  to
         delete.

     A  file with neither itself nor a marker present is silently skipped —— there is nothing to say
     about it. If this is true of both config.json and discovery.conf, a single 4mno24m 4mlegacy24m 4mconfigura‐0m
     4mtion24m 4mfound24m line is printed instead of two silent files and no output at all.

     Because the marker is a symlink keyed on the file’s 1mpath22m, not  its  content,  a  file  that  is
     deleted  and later replaced by a different, never-converted file at the same path (for example,
     a package rollback followed by a reinstall) makes the marker resolve again even though the  new
     file  itself  was never converted. This command does not try to detect that case —— when a file
     and a resolving marker are both present, it adds a note that the marker may be  stale  and  the
     file’s  contents  should  be verified against the INI configuration, so a human can decide. Use
     4mnvme24m 4mconfig24m 4mconvert24m if in doubt: converting an already-converted file is a safe no-op.

1mOPTIONS0m
1mGLOBAL OPTIONS0m
     The following options are defined at the top-level nvme command and are available to this  sub‐
     command:

     --dry-run
         Print the command that would be executed, but do not actually execute it.

     --no-ioctl-probing
         Disable probing for 64-bit IOCTL support.

     --no-retries
         Disable retry logic on transient errors.

     -o <fmt>, --output-format=<fmt>
         Set  the  reporting format to 4mnormal24m, 4mtabular,24m 4m'json24m, or 4mbinary24m. Only one output format may
         be used at a time.

     --output-format-version=<version>
         Select the output format version. Version 4m124m uses the original field naming, while version 4m20m
         (default) provides more consistent and script-friendly field names. Other versions are  re‐
         jected.

     --quiet
         Suppress  informational messages. Errors are still reported, and --quiet cancels any --ver‐
         bose for the library log level.

     --set-options=<key=value>[,<key=value>...]
         Set libnvme library options for this invocation. Supported keys are 4mforce-4k24m,  4mmi-probe-en‐0m
         4mabled24m, 4mtest-base-dir24m and 4mtest-sysfs-dir24m.

     --timeout=<ms>
         Set the timeout for the command in milliseconds.  4minfinite24m or 4m-124m waits without a time limit
         (0xffffffff).

     -v, --verbose
         Increase  the level of detail in the output. May be specified multiple times to further in‐
         crease verbosity.

     These options can also be set as machine-wide defaults in nvme-cli.conf(5). A command-line flag
     always overrides the file.

1mEXIT STATUS0m
     Returns 0 if neither legacy file has anything to report. Returns  a  non-zero  status  if  con‐
     fig.json  or  discovery.conf,  or  a  4m.converted24m marker for either, is present —— regardless of
     which of the states listed above applies. Use the printed output, not the exit status, to  tell
     those states apart.

1mEXAMPLES0m
     •   Check the system’s legacy configuration state, config.json already converted and no discov‐
         ery.conf ever present:

             # nvme config status

             /usr/local/etc/nvme/config.json: present, already converted (/usr/local/etc/nvme/config.json.converted exists) -- delete both once rollback is no longer a concern
             note: if /usr/local/etc/nvme/config.json was replaced after conversion (for example, a package rollback followed by reinstall), this marker may be stale; verify its contents against the INI configuration before deleting either file

     •   Check a system that never had a legacy configuration:

             # nvme config status

             no legacy configuration found; nothing to convert

     nvme-discover(1) 34m1mhttps://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/blob/master/libnvme/design/CONFIG.md0m

1mNAME0m

1mSYNOPSIS0m

                             [--config=<file> | -J <file>]
                             [--verbose | -v]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Parses and validates the NVMe-oF INI connection configuration file used by 4mnvme24m 4mconnect-all24m and

     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mdapustor24m 4msmart-log-add24m <device>

                             [--raw-binary | -b]
                             [--json | -j]

1mDESCRIPTION0m

     structure.

     /dev/nvme0), or a namespace block device (ex: /dev/nvme0n1).

     on  the  option flags; the structure may parsed by the program and printed in a readable format
     or the raw buffer may be printed to stdout for another program to parse.

         the device global SMART log. The broadcast value 0xffffffff can also be given as 4mall24m or 4m-124m.

         Set  libnvme library options for this invocation. Supported keys are 4mforce-4k24m, 4mmi-probe-en‐0m
         4mabled24m, 4mtest-base-dir24m and 4mtest-sysfs-dir24m.

         Set the timeout for the command in milliseconds.  4minfinite24m or 4m-124m waits without a time limit
         (0xffffffff).

1mNAME0m

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mexclusion24m 4madd24m [--name=<NAME> | -N <NAME>]
                             --entry=<ENTRY> | -e <ENTRY>

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Append  an  entry  to the NVMe-oF exclusion list named <NAME>, creating the list if it does not
     exist. The entry is a semicolon-separated list of key=value fields; a  controller  is  excluded
     when it matches every field present in the entry.

     The  recognized  field keys are the 4mnvme24m 4mconnect24m option names: transport, traddr, trsvcid, nqn,
     host-traddr, host-iface, hostnqn and hostid. Only the fields given are matched, so a single key
     excludes broadly and more keys narrow the  match.  See  the  exclusion  list  overview  (EXCLU‐
     SIONS.md) for the full match semantics.

     The  entry  is  validated before it is written; an entry with an unknown key, or with no recog‐
     nized field, is rejected. This command requires root.

1mOPTIONS0m
     -N <NAME>, --name=<NAME>
         Name of the exclusion list to add to. Omit to add to  the  default  list  (/etc/nvme/exclu‐
         sions.conf).

     -e <ENTRY>, --entry=<ENTRY>
         The entry to add, e.g. "transport=tcp;traddr=192.0.2.10;nqn=...".

     command:

     --dry-run
         Print the command that would be executed, but do not actually execute it.

         Disable probing for 64-bit IOCTL support.

         be used at a time.

         (default)  provides more consistent and script-friendly field names. Other versions are re‐
         jected.

         Suppress informational messages. Errors are still reported, and --quiet cancels any  --ver‐
         bose for the library log level.

     --set-options=<key=value>[,<key=value>...]
         Set  libnvme library options for this invocation. Supported keys are 4mforce-4k24m, 4mmi-probe-en‐0m
         4mabled24m, 4mtest-base-dir24m and 4mtest-sysfs-dir24m.

     --timeout=<ms>
         Set the timeout for the command in milliseconds.  4minfinite24m or 4m-124m waits without a time limit
         (0xffffffff).

     -v, --verbose
         Increase the level of detail in the output. May be specified multiple times to further  in‐
         crease verbosity.

     These options can also be set as machine-wide defaults in nvme-cli.conf(5). A command-line flag
     always overrides the file.

1mDESCRIPTION0m

     variable, in the same spirit as 4mvisudo24m or 4mcrontab24m 4m-e24m. A missing list is created.

     exits.  On  save the result is validated; if it contains a bad entry you are offered the chance

     changes are not saved, the scratch copy is kept and its path printed so your edits are recover‐
     able.

1mSYNOPSIS0m

                             [--nsid=<nsid> | -n <nsid>]
                             [--tler=<tler> | -t <tler>]
                             [--dulbe | -d]
                             [--sel=<select> | -S <select>] [--save | -s]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Get and set the error recovery feature.

     /dev/nvme0), or a namespace block device (ex: /dev/nvme0n1). If the character device is  given,
     the  '--nsid'  option  is  mandatory,  otherwise it will use the ns-id of the namespace for the
     block device you opened. For block devices, the ns-id used can be overridden with the same  op‐
     tion.

     If  any  of  the setting options (--tler or --dulbe) are specified, the command will update the
     error recovery configuration for the specified namespace. If neither option  is  specified,  it
     will retrieve and display the current configuration.

     On success it returns 0, error code otherwise.

1mOPTIONS0m
     -n <nsid>, --nsid=<nsid>

         overrides the block nsid if given. The broadcast value 0xffffffff can also be given as  4mall0m
         or 4m-124m.

     -t <tler>, --tler=<tler>
         Time  limited  error  recovery  value.  Indicaes  the limited retry time in 100 millisecond
         units.

     -d, --dulbe
         Deallocated or unwritten logical block error enable.

     -S <select>, --sel=<select>
         Select (SEL): This field specifies which value of the attributes to return in the  provided
         data:  allbox  tab(:);  lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt lt.  T{ Select T}:T{ Name
         T}:T{ Description T} T{ 0 T}:T{ current T}:T{ Current T} T{ 1 T}:T{ default  T}:T{  Default
         T} T{ 2 T}:T{ saved T}:T{ Saved T} T{ 3 T}:T{ supported T}:T{ Supported capabilities T}


     -s, --save
         Save the attribute so that it persists through all power states and resets.

     The  following options are defined at the top-level nvme command and are available to this sub‐
     command:

     --dry-run
         Print the command that would be executed, but do not actually execute it.

     --no-ioctl-probing
         Disable probing for 64-bit IOCTL support.

     --no-retries
         Disable retry logic on transient errors.

     -o <fmt>, --output-format=<fmt>
         Set the reporting format to 4mnormal24m, 4mtabular,24m 4m'json24m, or 4mbinary24m. Only one output  format  may
         be used at a time.

     --output-format-version=<version>
         Select the output format version. Version 4m124m uses the original field naming, while version 4m20m
         (default)  provides more consistent and script-friendly field names. Other versions are re‐
         jected.

     --quiet
         Suppress informational messages. Errors are still reported, and --quiet cancels any  --ver‐
         bose for the library log level.

         Set  libnvme library options for this invocation. Supported keys are 4mforce-4k24m, 4mmi-probe-en‐0m
         4mabled24m, 4mtest-base-dir24m and 4mtest-sysfs-dir24m.

     --timeout=<ms>
         Set the timeout for the command in milliseconds.  4minfinite24m or 4m-124m waits without a time limit
         (0xffffffff).

         Increase the level of detail in the output. May be specified multiple times to further  in‐
         crease verbosity.

     always overrides the file.

     •   Has the program issue a feat err-recovery to get the current configuration:

             # nvme feat err-recovery /dev/nvme0n1

         given more than once.

                             [--keyring=<name> | -k <name>]
                             [--keytype=<type> | -t <type>]
                             [--identity=<identity> | -i <identity>]

     Checks   if   the   given   string   is   a   valid  KX-HMAC-CHAP  host  secret  of  the  form:
     DHHC-1:00:ia6zGodOr4SEG0Zzaw398rpY0wqipUWj4jWjUh4HWUz6aQ2n: and prints the  hash  algorithm  it
     records, the secret length, and the CRC.

     If  4m--keydata24m  is  not given the secret is read from stdin, which also allows checking a secret
     stored in a file, e.g. 4mnvme24m 4mkeys24m 4mcheck-kxchap-secret24m 4m<24m 4mkeyfile24m.

     If 4m--identity24m is given the specified keyring is also checked for a secret already stored  under
     that  identity  (as inserted by 1mnvme-keys-import22m(1)); the result (not loaded, loaded and match‐
     ing, or loaded but different) is reported. This command never modifies the keyring.

     Looking up a secret requires the 4mkxchap24m keyring key type, which is not yet provided by any  re‐
     leased Linux kernel; see 1mnvme-keys-import22m(1) for details.

1mNAME0m

                             [--keytype=<type> | -t <type>]

                             [--keydata=<key> | -d <key>]

     4mNVMeTLSkey-1:<hmac>:<base64-encoded24m 4mdata>:24m and prints the hash  function  it  records  and  the
     length of the PSK.

     keyring is checked for a TLS PSK already stored under that identity; the result (loaded or not,
     with  its serial number if loaded) is reported. This command never modifies the keyring; to in‐
     sert a TLS PSK use 1mnvme-keys-insert-tls-psk22m(1).

         Name of the keyring to check for an already loaded TLS PSK. Default is 4m.nvme24m.

     self in PSK interchange format 4mNVMeTLSkey-1:<hmac>:<base6424m 4mencoded24m 4mdata>:24m. Each key is exported

     1mkeys-insert-tls-psk22m(1) or 1mnvme-keys-check-tls-psk22m(1).

1mNAME0m
     nvme-keys-gen-tls-psk - Generate a NVMe TLS PSK

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     4mnvme24m [<global-options>] 4mkeys24m 4mgen-tls-psk24m [--keyring=<name> | -k <name>]
                             [--keytype=<type> | -t <type>]
                             [--hostnqn=<nqn> | -n <nqn>]
                             [--subsysnqn=<nqn> | -c <nqn>]
                             [--hmac=<hmac-id> | -m <hmac-id>]
                             [--identity=<id-vers> | -I <id-vers>]
                             [--secret=<secret> | -s <secret>]
                             [--insert | -i]
                             [--compat | -C]
                             [--keyfile=<keyfile> | -f <keyfile>]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Generate   a   NVMe   TLS   configured   PSK  and  print  it  in  the  PSK  interchange  format
     4mNVMeTLSkey-1:<hmac>:<base6424m 4mencoded24m 4mdata>:24m. If the 4m--insert24m option is given a retained  PSK  is
     additionally  derived from the configured PSK and the host NQN, using the HKDF-Expand-Label al‐
     gorithm from RFC 8446, the TLS PSK is derived from it, and that  is  stored  in  the  specified
     keyring  under an identity computed from the host NQN and the subsystem NQN: 4mNVMe0R<hmac>24m 4m<host0m
     4mNQN>24m 4m<subsystem24m 4mNQN>24m (for identity version 4m024m) or 4mNVMe1R<hmac>24m 4m<host24m 4mNQN>24m 4m<subsystem24m  4mNQN>24m  4m<PSK0m
     4mdigest>24m  (for identity version 4m124m). Once the TLS PSK is stored in the keyring the configured PSK
     it was derived from cannot be retrieved from the keyring.

     The diagnostics that validate 4m--secret24m are printed to stdout rather than stderr. Most  of  them
     accompany  a  non-zero  exit,  but 4mSkipping24m 4mexcess24m 4msecret24m 4mbytes24m does not: an over-long 4m--secret0m
     still exits 0, with the warning sitting ahead of the key, so a script reading the key off  std‐
     out gets the warning instead.

     Both  NQNs  are  inputs to the TLS PSK itself, not just to the identity it is stored under: the
     host NQN through the retained PSK derivation, and both NQNs again through the  identity  (iden‐
     tity  version  4m024m) or the PSK digest it embeds (identity version 4m124m), which is the context of the
     TLS PSK derivation.

1mOPTIONS0m
     -k <name>, --keyring=<name>
         Name of the keyring into which the TLS PSK should be stored. Default is 4m.nvme24m.

     -t <type>, --keytype=<type>
         Type of the key under which the TLS PSK is stored. Default is 4mpsk24m.

     -n <nqn>, --hostnqn=<nqn>
         Host NVMe Qualified Name (NQN) to be used for the retained PSK derivation and for the iden‐
         tity the TLS PSK is stored under. Defaults to  the  host  NQN  of  the  system,  read  from
         /etc/nvme/hostnqn or, if that file does not exist, generated from the host ID.

     -c <nqn>, --subsysnqn=<nqn>
         Subsystem  NVMe  Qualified Name (NQN) to be used for the identity the TLS PSK is stored un‐
         der. Required with --insert.

     -m <hmac-id>, --hmac=<hmac-id>
         Select the hash function. It derives the retained PSK and identifies  the  TLS  1.3  cipher
         suite  the TLS PSK is bound to, so it is recorded both in the PSK interchange format and in
         the TLS PSK identity, written as two digits  (4m<hmac>24m  above).  Possible  values  are:  1  -
         SHA-256 (default) 2 - SHA-384

     -I <id-vers>, --identity=<id-vers>
         Select  the  TLS PSK identity version of the identity the TLS PSK is stored under. Possible
         values are: 0 - Obsolete (default); defined in the NVMe TCP Transport Specification 1.0 1 -
         TLS 1.3 with the PSK digest in the TLS PSK identity

     -s <secret>, --secret=<secret>
         Configured PSK (in hexadecimal) to be used. If none are provided a random value is used.

     -i, --insert
         Additionally derive a retained PSK and, from that, the TLS PSK, and insert the TLS PSK into
         the keyring. The configured PSK is printed in PSK interchange format either way.

     -C, --compat
         Use the original non-RFC 8446 compliant algorithm when deriving the retained  PSK  and  the
         TLS PSK for compatibility with older implementations.

     -f <keyfile>, --keyfile=<keyfile>
         Append  the  identity  of the TLS PSK, and the TLS PSK itself in PSK interchange format, to
         keyfile. Ignored without --insert, which is what derives the TLS PSK.

1mGLOBAL OPTIONS0m

     command:
