1mINPUT FORMATS0m
     1msfdisk 22msupports two input formats and generic header lines.

   1mHeader lines0m
     The optional header lines specify generic information that apply to the  partition  table.  The
     header-line format is:

     1m<name>: <value>0m

     The currently recognized headers are:

     1munit0m
         Specify the partitioning unit. The only supported unit is 1msectors22m.

     1mlabel0m
         Specify the partition table type. For example 1mdos 22mor 1mgpt22m.

     1mlabel-id0m
         Specify  the  partition table identifier. It should be a hexadecimal number (with a 0x pre‐
         fix) for MBR and a UUID for GPT.

     1mfirst-lba0m
         Specify the first usable sector for GPT partitions. This header is ignored  if  the  script
         and device sector size differ. In this case 1msfdisk 22muses label specific default.

     1mlast-lba0m
         Specify the last usable sector for GPT partitions. This header is ignored if the script and
         device  sector  size  differ. In this case 1msfdisk 22muses label specific default. The last-lba
         header is ignored if 1m--force 22mis specified, making the script usable on disks with different
         sizes.

     1mtable-length0m
         Specify the maximal number of GPT partitions.

     1mgrain0m
         Specify minimal size in bytes used to calculate partitions alignment. The default  is  1MiB
         and it’s strongly recommended to use the default. Do not modify this variable if you’re not
         sure.

     1msector-size0m
         Specifies  the sector size used in the input. 1msfdisk 22malways internally uses the device sec‐
         tor size provided by the kernel for the block device, or as specified by the  user  on  the
         command  line  (see  1m--sector-size22m).  Starting with version 2.39, 1msfdisk 22mrecalculates sizes
         from the input if the 1msector-size 22mheader and device sector size are different.

     Note that it is only possible to use header lines before the first partition  is  specified  in
     the input.

   1mUnnamed-fields format0m
        4mstart24m 4msize24m 4mtype24m 4mbootable0m

     where each line fills one partition descriptor.

     Fields  are  separated  by  whitespace,  comma  (recommended) or semicolon possibly followed by
     whitespace; initial and trailing whitespace is ignored. Numbers can be octal, decimal or  hexa‐
     decimal;  decimal  is  the default. When a field is absent, empty or specified as '-' a default
     value is used. But when the 1m-N 22moption (change a single partition) is  given,  the  default  for
     each field is its previous value.

     The  default  value  of  4mstart24m is the first non-assigned sector aligned according to device I/O
     limits. The default start offset for the first partition is 1 MiB. If the offset is followed by
     the multiplicative suffixes (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB, EiB, ZiB and YiB), then the number is in‐
     terpreted as offset in bytes. Since v2.38 when the 1m-N 22moption (change  a  single  partition)  is
     given, a '+' can be used to enlarge partition by move start of the partition if there is a free
     space before the partition.

     The  default  value  of 4msize24m indicates "as much as possible"; i.e., until the next partition or
     end-of-device. A numerical argument is by default interpreted as a number of  sectors,  however
     if  the  size  is followed by one of the multiplicative suffixes (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB, EiB,
     ZiB and YiB) then the number is interpreted as the size of the partition in  bytes  and  it  is
     then  aligned  according to the device I/O limits. A '+' can be used instead of a number to en‐
     large the partition as much as possible. Note '+' is equivalent to the default behaviour for  a
     new partition; existing partitions will be resized as required.

     The partition 4mtype24m is given in hex for MBR (DOS) where 0x prefix is optional; a GUID string for
     GPT;  a  shortcut  or  an alias. It’s recommended to use two letters for MBR hex codes to avoid
     collision between deprecated shortcut 'E' and '0E' MBR hex  code.  For  backward  compatibility
     1msfdisk 22mtries to interpret 4mtype24m as a shortcut as a first possibility in partitioning scripts al‐
     though on other places (e.g. 1m--part-type 22mcommand) it tries shortcuts as the last possibility.

     Since  v2.36 libfdisk supports partition type aliases as extension to shortcuts. The alias is a
     simple human readable word (e.g. "linux").

     Since v2.37 libfdisk supports partition type names on input, ignoring the case of  the  charac‐
     ters  and  all  non-alphanumeric and non-digit characters in the name (e.g. "Linux /usr x86" is
     the same as "linux usr-x86").

     Supported shortcuts and aliases:

     1mL - alias 'linux'0m
         Linux; means 83 for MBR and 0FC63DAF-8483-4772-8E79-3D69D8477DE4 for GPT.

     1mS - alias 'swap'0m
         swap area; means 82 for MBR and 0657FD6D-A4AB-43C4-84E5-0933C84B4F4F for GPT

     1mEx - alias 'extended'0m
         MBR extended partition; means 05 for MBR. The original shortcut 'E' is  deprecated  due  to
         collision with 0x0E MBR partition type.

     1mH - alias 'home'0m
         home partition; means 933AC7E1-2EB4-4F13-B844-0E14E2AEF915 for GPT

     1mU - alias 'uefi'0m
         EFI System partition, means EF for MBR and C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B for GPT

     1mR - alias 'raid'0m
         Linux RAID; means FD for MBR and A19D880F-05FC-4D3B-A006-743F0F84911E for GPT

     1mV - alias 'lvm'0m
         LVM; means 8E for MBR and E6D6D379-F507-44C2-A23C-238F2A3DF928 for GPT

     The default 4mtype24m value is 4mlinux24m.

     The shortcut 'X' for Linux extended partition (85) is deprecated in favour of 'Ex'.

     4mbootable24m is specified as [1m*22m|1m-22m], with as default not-bootable. The value of this field is irrel‐
     evant  for  Linux  -  when Linux runs it has been booted already - but it might play a role for
     certain boot loaders and for other operating systems.

   1mNamed-fields format0m
     This format is more readable, robust, extensible and allows specifying  additional  information
     (e.g., a UUID). It is recommended to use this format to keep your scripts more readable.

        [4mdevice24m 1m:22m] 4mname24m[1m=4m22mvalue24m], ...

     The 4mdevice24m field is optional. 1msfdisk 22mextracts the partition number from the device name. It al‐
     lows  specifying  the  partitions in random order. This functionality is mostly used by 1m--dump22m.
     Don’t use it if you are not sure.

     The 4mvalue24m can be between quotation marks (e.g., name="This  is  partition  name").  The  fields
     1mstart= 22mand 1msize= 22msupport '+' and '-' in the same way as 1mUnnamed-fields format22m.

     The currently supported fields are:

     1mstart=4m22mnumber0m
         The  first  non-assigned  sector  aligned according to device I/O limits. The default start
         offset for the first partition is 1 MiB. If the offset is followed  by  the  multiplicative
         suffixes  (KiB,  MiB,  GiB,  TiB, PiB, EiB, ZiB and YiB), then the number is interpreted as
         offset in bytes.

     1msize=4m22mnumber0m
         Specify the partition size in sectors. The number may be  followed  by  the  multiplicative
         suffixes  (KiB,  MiB,  GiB,  TiB,  PiB, EiB, ZiB and YiB), then it’s interpreted as size in
         bytes and the size is aligned according to device I/O limits.

     1mbootable0m
         Mark the partition as bootable.

     1mattrs=4m22mstring0m
         Partition attributes, usually GPT partition attribute bits. See 1m--part-attrs 22mfor  more  de‐
         tails about the GPT-bits string format.

     1muuid=4m22mstring0m
         GPT partition UUID.

     1mname=4m22mstring0m
         GPT partition name.

     1mtype=4m22mcode0m
         A  hexadecimal  number  (without  0x)  for  an MBR partition, a GUID for a GPT partition, a
         shortcut as for unnamed-fields format or a type name (e.g. type="Linux  /usr  (x86)").  See
         above  the  section about the unnamed-fields format for more details. For backward compati‐
         bility the 1mId= 22mfield has the same meaning.

1mEMPTY DISK LABEL0m
     1msfdisk 22mdoes not create partition table without partitions by default. The lines with partitions
     are expected in the script by default. The empty partition table has to be explicitly requested
     by "label: <name>" script header line without any partitions lines. For example:

        1mecho 'label: gpt' | sfdisk /dev/sdb0m

     creates empty GPT partition table. Note that the 1m--append 22mdisables this feature.

1mBACKING UP THE PARTITION TABLE0m
     It is recommended to save the layout of your devices. 1msfdisk 22msupports two ways.

   1mDump in sfdisk compatible format0m
     Use the 1m--dump 22mcommand to save a description of the device layout to a text file. The dump for‐
     mat is suitable for later 1msfdisk 22minput. For example:

        1msfdisk --dump /dev/sda > sda.dump0m

     This can later be restored by:

        1msfdisk /dev/sda < sda.dump0m

     Note that 1msfdisk 22mcompletely restores partition types and partition  UUIDs.  This  could  poten‐
     tially become problematic if you duplicate the same layout to different disks, as it may result
     in duplicate UUIDs within your system.

   1mFull binary backup0m
     If you want to do a full binary backup of all sectors where the partition table is stored, then
     use  the  1m--backup-pt-sectors  22mcommand. It writes the sectors to 4m~/sfdisk-<device>-<offset>.bak0m
     files. The default name of the backup file can be changed with the  1m--backup-file  22moption.  The
     backup files contain only raw data from the 4mdevice24m. For example:

        1msfdisk --backup-pt-sectors /dev/sda0m

     The GPT header can later be restored by:

        1mdd if=~/sfdisk-sda-0x00000200.bak of=/dev/sda seek=$((0x00000200)) bs=1 conv=notrunc0m

     It’s  also  possible  to  use  the  1m--backup 22moption to create the same backup immediately after
     startup for other 1msfdisk 22mcommands. For example, backup partition table before deleting all par‐
     titions from partition table:

        1msfdisk --backup --delete /dev/sda0m

     The same concept of backup files is used by 1mwipefs22m(8).

     Note that 1msfdisk 22msince version 2.26 no longer provides the 1m-I 22moption to restore sectors.  1mdd22m(1)
     provides all necessary functionality.

1mCOLORS0m
     The output colorization is implemented by 1mterminal-colors.d22m(5) functionality. Implicit coloring
     can be disabled by an empty file

        4m/etc/terminal-colors.d/sfdisk.disable0m

     for the 1msfdisk 22mcommand or for all tools by

        4m/etc/terminal-colors.d/disable0m

     Since version 2.41, the $NO_COLOR environment variable is also supported to disable output col‐
     orization unless explicitly enabled by a command-line option.

     The  user-specific  4m$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/terminal-colors.d24m or 4m$HOME/.config/terminal-colors.d24m over‐
     rides the global setting.

     Note that the output colorization may be enabled by default, and in this case 4mterminal-colors.d0m
     directories do not have to exist yet.

     The logical color names supported by 1msfdisk 22mare:

     1mheader0m
         The header of the output tables.

     1mwarn0m
         The warning messages.

     1mwelcome0m
         The welcome message.

1mENVIRONMENT0m
     1mSFDISK_DEBUG22m=all
         enables 1msfdisk 22mdebug output.

     1mLIBFDISK_DEBUG22m=all
         enables libfdisk debug output.

     1mLIBBLKID_DEBUG22m=all
         enables libblkid debug output.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_DEBUG22m=all
         enables libsmartcols debug output.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_DEBUG_PADDING22m=on
         use visible padding characters.

     1mLIBSMARTCOLS_JSON22m=compact|lines
         Controls JSON output format when using 1m--json22m. Supported values are 1mcompact 22mfor JSON output
         with minimal whitespace, and 1mlines 22mfor JSON Lines format (one JSON object per line). If un‐
         set or set to any other value, pretty-printed JSON is used.

     1mLOCK_BLOCK_DEVICE22m=<mode>
         use exclusive BSD lock. The mode is "1" or "0". See 1m--lock 22mfor more details.

1mNOTES0m
     Since version 2.26 1msfdisk 22mno longer provides the 1m-R 22mor 1m--re-read 22moption to force the kernel  to
     reread the partition table. Use 1mblockdev --rereadpt 22minstead.

     Since  version  2.26  1msfdisk  22mdoes  not  provide  the  1m--DOS22m,  1m--IBM22m, 1m--DOS-extended22m, 1m--unhide22m,
     1m--show-extended22m, 1m--cylinders22m, 1m--heads22m, 1m--sectors22m, 1m--inside-outer22m, 1m--not-inside-outer 22moptions.

1mEXAMPLES0m
     1msfdisk --list --label-nested=mbr /dev/sda0m
         Print protective MBR on device with GPT disk label.

     1mecho -e ',10M,L\n,10M,L\n,+,\n' | sfdisk /dev/sdc0m
         Create three Linux partitions, with the default start, the size of the first two partitions
         is 10MiB, and the last partition fills all available space on the device.

     1mecho -e 'size=10M, type=L\n size=10M, type=L\n size=+\n' | sfdisk /dev/sdc0m
         The same as the previous example, but in named-fields format.

     1mecho -e 'type=swap' | sfdisk -N 3 /dev/sdc0m
         Set type of the 3rd partition to 'swap'.

     1msfdisk --part-type /dev/sdc 3 swap0m
         The same as the previous example, but without script use.

     1msfdisk --delete /dev/sdc 20m
         Delete 2nd partition.

     1mecho "+,+" | sfdisk -N 3 --move-data /dev/sdc0m
         Enlarge 3rd partition in both directions, move start to use free space before the partition
         and enlarge the size to use all free space after to the partition, and move partition  data
         too.

1mAUTHORS0m
     34mKarel Zak 0m<kzak@redhat.com>

     The current 1msfdisk 22mimplementation is based on the original 1msfdisk 22mfrom Andries E. Brouwer.

1mSEE ALSO0m
     1mfdisk22m(8), 1mcfdisk22m(8), 1mparted22m(8), 1mpartprobe22m(8), 1mpartx22m(8)

1mREPORTING BUGS0m
     For bug reports, use the 34missue tracker 0m<https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/issues>.

1mAVAILABILITY0m
     The  1msfdisk 22mcommand is part of the util-linux package which can be downloaded from 34mLinux Kernel0m
     34mArchive 0m<https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/utils/util-linux/>.

=======
smpdump
=======

--------------------------------------------
dump InfiniBand subnet management attributes
--------------------------------------------

:Date: 2017-08-21
:Manual section: 8
:Manual group: Open IB Diagnostics

SYNOPSIS
========

smpdump [options] <dlid|dr_path> <attribute> [attribute_modifier]

DESCRIPTION
===========

smpdump is a general purpose SMP utility which gets SM attributes from a
specified SMA. The result is dumped in hex by default.

OPTIONS
=======

**dlid|drpath**
        LID or DR path to SMA

**attribute**
        IBA attribute ID for SM attribute

**attribute_modifier**
        IBA modifier for SM attribute

**-s, --string**
        Print strings in packet if possible


Addressing Flags
----------------

.. Define the common option -D for Directed routes

**-D, --Direct**     The address specified is a directed route
::

    Examples:
       [options] -D [options] "0"          # self port
       [options] -D [options] "0,1,2,1,4"  # out via port 1, then 2, ...

       (Note the second number in the path specified must match the port being
       used.  This can be specified using the port selection flag '-P' or the
       port found through the automatic selection process.)


.. Define the common option -L

**-L, --Lid**   The address specified is a LID


Port Selection flags
--------------------

.. Define the common option -C

**-C, --Ca <ca_name>**    use the specified ca_name.


.. Define the common option -P

**-P, --Port <ca_port>**    use the specified ca_port.


.. Define the common option -Y

**-Y, --pkey-idx <idx>**
  P_Key table index (0-65535, default 0) used for the outgoing SA/GMP MADs.
  SMP (SMI directed-route/LID-routed) MADs always use P_Key index 0.

.. Explanation of local port selection

Local port Selection
--------------------

Multiple port/Multiple CA support: when no IB device or port is specified
(see the "local umad parameters" below), the libibumad library
selects the port to use by the following criteria:

	1. the first port that is ACTIVE.
	2. if not found, the first port that is UP (physical link up).

	If a port and/or CA name is specified, the libibumad library attempts
	to fulfill the user request, and will fail if it is not possible.

	For example:

        ::

	    ibaddr                 # use the first port (criteria #1 above)
	    ibaddr -C mthca1       # pick the best port from "mthca1" only.
	    ibaddr -P 2            # use the second (active/up) port from the first available IB device.
	    ibaddr -C mthca0 -P 2  # use the specified port only.


Debugging flags
---------------

.. Define the common option -d

-d
        raise the IB debugging level.
        May be used several times (-ddd or -d -d -d).


.. Define the common option -e

-e      show send and receive errors (timeouts and others)

.. Define the common option -h

**-h, --help**      show the usage message


.. Define the common option -v

**-v, --verbose**
        increase the application verbosity level.
        May be used several times (-vv or -v -v -v)


.. Define the common option -V

**-V, --version**     show the version info.


Configuration flags
-------------------

.. Define the common option -t

**-t, --timeout <timeout_ms>** override the default timeout for the solicited mads.


.. Define the common option -z

**--config, -z  <config_file>** Specify alternate config file.

        Default: @IBDIAG_CONFIG_PATH@/ibdiag.conf


FILES
=====

.. Common text for the config file

CONFIG FILE
-----------

@IBDIAG_CONFIG_PATH@/ibdiag.conf

A global config file is provided to set some of the common options for all
tools.  See supplied config file for details.


EXAMPLES
========

Direct Routed Examples

::

        smpdump -D 0,1,2,3,5 16 # NODE DESC
        smpdump -D 0,1,2 0x15 2 # PORT INFO, port 2

LID Routed Examples

::

        smpdump 3 0x15 2        # PORT INFO, lid 3 port 2
        smpdump 0xa0 0x11       # NODE INFO, lid 0xa0

SEE ALSO
========

smpquery (8)


AUTHOR
======

Hal Rosenstock
        < halr@voltaire.com >

4mSPLIT24m(1)                                    User Commands                                   4mSPLIT24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     split - split a file into pieces

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     1msplit 22m[4mOPTION24m]... [4mFILE24m [4mPREFIX24m]]

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     Output  pieces of FILE to PREFIXaa, PREFIXab, ...; default size is 1000 lines, and default PRE‐
     FIX is 'x'.

     With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

     Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-a1m-a, --suffix-length=N22m8;;
            generate suffixes of length N (default 2)

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split--additional-suffix1m--additional-suffix=SUFFIX22m8;;
            append an additional SUFFIX to file names

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-b1m-b, --bytes=SIZE22m8;;
            put SIZE bytes per output file

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-C1m-C, --line-bytes=SIZE22m8;;
            put at most SIZE bytes of records per output file

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-d1m-d22m8;;     use numeric suffixes starting at 0, not alphabetic

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split--numeric-suffixes1m--numeric-suffixes[=FROM]22m8;;
            same as 1m-d22m, but allow setting the start value

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-x1m-x22m8;;     use hex suffixes starting at 0, not alphabetic

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split--hex-suffixes1m--hex-suffixes[=FROM]22m8;;
            same as 1m-x22m, but allow setting the start value

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-e1m-e, --elide-empty-files22m8;;
            do not generate empty output files with '-n'

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split--filter1m--filter=COMMAND22m8;;
            write to shell COMMAND; file name is $FILE

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-l1m-l, --lines=NUMBER22m8;;
            put NUMBER lines/records per output file

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-n1m-n, --number=CHUNKS22m8;;
            generate CHUNKS output files; see explanation below

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-t1m-t, --separator=SEP22m8;;
            use SEP instead of newline as the record separator; '\0' (zero) specifies the NUL  char‐
            acter

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split-u1m-u, --unbuffered22m8;;
            immediately copy input to output with '-n r/...'

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html#split--verbose1m--verbose22m8;;
            print a diagnostic just before each output file is opened

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/split#split--help1m--help22m8;;
            display this help and exit

     8;;https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/split#split--version1m--version22m8;;
            output version information and exit

     The  SIZE  argument  is  an  integer  and  optional  unit (example: 10K is 10*1024).  Units are
     K,M,G,T,P,E,Z,Y,R,Q (powers of 1024) or KB,MB,... (powers of 1000).   Binary  prefixes  can  be
     used, too: KiB=K, MiB=M, and so on.

   1mCHUNKS may be:0m
     N       split into N files based on size of input
     K/N     output Kth of N to standard output
     l/N     split into N files without splitting lines/records
     l/K/N   output Kth of N to standard output without splitting lines/records
     r/N     like 'l' but use round robin distribution
     r/K/N   likewise but only output Kth of N to standard output

     1m-n  22m(except 1m-nr22m) will buffer to $TMPDIR, defaulting to 4m/tmp24m, if the input size cannot easily be
     determined.

1mAUTHOR0m
     Written by Torbjorn Granlund and Richard M. Stallman.

     Report any translation bugs to: <https://translationproject.org/team/>.
     GNU coreutils home page: <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/>

     Full documentation <https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/split>

4mSSH-AGENT24m(1)                           General Commands Manual                          4mSSH-AGENT24m(1)

1mNAME0m
     1mssh-agent 22m—— OpenSSH authentication agent

1mSYNOPSIS0m
     1mssh-agent 22m[1m-c 22m| 1m-s22m] [1m-DdU22m] [1m-T 22m| 1m-A 4m22mdirectory24m | 1m-a 4m22mbind_address24m] [1m-E 4m22mfingerprint_hash24m]
               [1m-O 4m22moption24m] [1m-P 4m22mallowed_providers24m] [1m-t 4m22mlife24m]
     1mssh-agent 22m[1m-U22m] [1m-T 22m| 1m-A 4m22mdirectory24m | 1m-a 4m22mbind_address24m] [1m-E 4m22mfingerprint_hash24m] [1m-O 4m22moption24m]
               [1m-P 4m22mallowed_providers24m] [1m-t 4m22mlife24m] 4mcommand24m [4marg24m ...]
     1mssh-agent 22m[1m-c 22m| 1m-s22m] 1m-k0m
     1mssh-agent -u0m
     1mssh-agent -V0m

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     1mssh-agent 22mis a program to hold private keys used for public key authentication.  Through use of
     environment  variables  the agent can be located and automatically used for authentication when
     logging in to other machines using 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;.

     The options are as follows:

     1m-a 4m22mbind_address0m
             Bind the agent to the Unix-domain socket 4mbind_address24m.  The  default  is  to  create  a
             socket in the 4m$HOME/.ssh/agent24m directory using a random path matching 4ms.*24m.

     1m-A 4m22msocket_path0m
             Specify  a  different  directory path under which to create the socket.  Sockets may be
             created in either a shared location or a user-specific directory.  User-specific direc‐
             tories are specified by prefixing the path name with 1muser:22m.  1mssh-agent 22mwill ensure  the
             directory  exists  and  create the listening socket directly in it.  Relative user-spe‐
             cific directory paths will be created to the user's 4m$HOME24m.

             Shared directories may be specified by prefixing an absolute path  name  with  1mshared:22m.
             In  this  case,  a temporary subdirectory will be created under the specified directory
             and the listening agent socket will be created in that.

             This option accepts the tokens described in the 8;;man:sshd_config(5)4msshd_config24m(5)8;; “TOKENS” section.

     1m-c      22mGenerate C-shell commands on standard output.  This is the default if 4mSHELL24m looks  like
             it's a csh style of shell.

     1m-D      22mForeground mode.  When this option is specified, 1mssh-agent 22mwill not fork.

     1m-d      22mDebug  mode.  When this option is specified, 1mssh-agent 22mwill not fork and will write de‐
             bug information to standard error.

     1m-E 4m22mfingerprint_hash0m
             Specifies the hash algorithm used when displaying key fingerprints.  Valid options are:
             “md5” and “sha256”.  The default is “sha256”.

     1m-k      22mKill the current agent (given by the 4mSSH_AGENT_PID24m environment variable).

     1m-O 4m22moption0m
             Specify  an   option   when   starting   1mssh-agent22m.    The   supported   options   are:
             1mallow-remote-pkcs1122m, 1mno-restrict-websafe 22mand 1mwebsafe-allow22m.

             The  1mallow-remote-pkcs11 22moption allows clients of a forwarded 1mssh-agent 22mto load PKCS#11
             or FIDO provider libraries.  By default only local clients may perform this  operation.
             Note that signalling that an 1mssh-agent 22mclient is remote is performed by 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;, and use
             of other tools to forward access to the agent socket may circumvent this restriction.

             The 1mno-restrict-websafe 22moption instructs 1mssh-agent 22mto permit signatures using FIDO keys
             that might be web authentication requests.  By default, 1mssh-agent 22mrefuses signature re‐
             quests  for  FIDO  keys where the key application string does not start with “ssh:” and
             when the data to be signed does not appear to be an 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; user authentication  request
             or  an  8;;man:ssh-keygen(1)4mssh-keygen24m(1)8;;  signature.  The default behaviour prevents forwarded access to a
             FIDO key from also implicitly forwarding the ability to authenticate to websites.

             Alternately the 1mwebsafe-allow 22moption allows specifying a pattern-list of  key  applica‐
             tion   strings   to   replace   the   default   application  allow-list,  for  example:
             “websafe-allow=ssh:*,example.org,*.example.com”

             See PATTERNS in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for a description of pattern-list syntax.

     1m-P 4m22mallowed_providers0m
             Specify a pattern-list of acceptable paths for PKCS#11 provider and FIDO  authenticator
             middleware  shared  libraries that may be used with the 1m-S 22mor 1m-s 22moptions to 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;;.
             Libraries that do not match the pattern list will be  refused.   The  default  list  is
             “/usr/lib*/*,/usr/local/lib*/*”.

             See PATTERNS in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for a description of pattern-list syntax.

     1m-s      22mGenerate  Bourne  shell commands on standard output.  This is the default if 4mSHELL24m does
             not look like it's a csh style of shell.

     1m-T      22mBind   the   agent   socket   in   a    randomised    subdirectory    of    the    form
             4m$TMPDIR/ssh-XXXXXXXXXX/agent.<ppid>24m,  instead  of the default behaviour of using a ran‐
             domised name matching 4m$HOME/.ssh/agent/s.*24m.

     1m-t 4m22mlife0m
             Set a default value for the maximum lifetime of identities added  to  the  agent.   The
             lifetime  may  be specified in seconds or in a time format specified in 8;;man:sshd_config(5)4msshd_config24m(5)8;;.
             A lifetime specified for an identity with 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;;  overrides  this  value.   Without
             this option the default maximum lifetime is forever.

     1m-U      22mInstructs 1mssh-agent 22mnot to clean up stale agent sockets under 4m$HOME/.ssh/agent/24m.

     1m-u      22mInstructs  1mssh-agent  22mto  only clean up stale agent sockets under 4m$HOME/.ssh/agent/24m and
             then exit immediately.  If this option is given  twice,  1mssh-agent  22mwill  delete  stale
             agent sockets regardless of the host name that created them.

     4mcommand24m [4marg24m 4m...24m]
             If a command (and optional arguments) is given, this is executed as a subprocess of the
             agent.  The agent exits automatically when the command given on the command line termi‐
             nates.

     1m-V      22mDisplay the version number and exit.

     There  are  three main ways to get an agent set up.  The first is at the start of an X session,
     where all other windows or programs are started as children  of  the  1mssh-agent  22mprogram.   The
     agent  starts  a  command  under  which  its  environment  variables  are exported, for example
     1mssh-agent xterm &22m.  When the command terminates, so does the agent.

     The second method is used for a login session.  When 1mssh-agent 22mis started, it prints the  shell
     commands required to set its environment variables, which in turn can be evaluated in the call‐
     ing shell, for example 1meval ‘ssh-agent -s‘22m.

     In  both of these cases, 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; looks at these environment variables and uses them to establish
     a connection to the agent.

     The third way to run 1mssh-agent 22mis via socket activation from a  supervising  process,  such  as
     systemd.  In this mode, the supervising process creates the listening socket and is responsible
     for  starting  1mssh-agent  22mas needed, and also for communicating the location of the socket lis‐
     tener to other programs in the user's session.  Socket activation is  used  when  1mssh-agent  22mis
     started  with  either  of  the  1m-d 22mor 1m-D 22mflags, no socket listening address specified by the 1m-a0m
     flag, and both the 4mLISTEN_FDS24m and 4mLISTEN_PID24m environment variables correctly  supplied  by  the
     supervising process.

     The  agent  initially  does  not  have any private keys.  Keys are added using 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;; or by
     8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; when 1mAddKeysToAgent 22mis set in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;;.   Multiple  identities  may  be  stored  in
     1mssh-agent  22mconcurrently  and 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will automatically use them if present.  8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;; is also
     used to remove keys from 1mssh-agent 22mand to query the keys that are held in one.

     Connections to 1mssh-agent 22mmay be forwarded from further remote hosts  using  the  1m-A  22moption  to
     8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  (but  see the caveats documented therein), avoiding the need for authentication data to
     be stored on other machines.  Authentication passphrases and private keys  never  go  over  the
     network: the connection to the agent is forwarded over SSH remote connections and the result is
     returned to the requester, allowing the user access to their identities anywhere in the network
     in a secure fashion.

     1mssh-agent 22mwill delete all keys it has loaded upon receiving SIGUSR1.

1mENVIRONMENT0m
     4mSSH_AGENT_PID24m  When  1mssh-agent  22mstarts,  it  stores the name of the agent's process ID (PID) in
                    this variable.

     4mSSH_AUTH_SOCK24m  When 1mssh-agent 22mstarts, it creates a Unix-domain socket and stores  its  pathname
                    in  this  variable.   It  is  accessible only to the current user, but is easily
                    abused by root or another instance of the same user.

1mFILES0m
     4m$HOME/.ssh/agent/s.*0m
             Unix-domain sockets used to contain the connection to the authentication agent.   These
             sockets should only be readable by the owner.  The sockets should get automatically re‐
             moved when the agent exits.

1mSEE ALSO0m
     8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;, 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;;, 8;;man:ssh-keygen(1)4mssh-keygen24m(1)8;;, 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;;, 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;

1mAUTHORS0m
     OpenSSH  is  a  derivative  of  the original and free ssh 1.2.12 release by Tatu Ylonen.  Aaron
     Campbell, Bob Beck, Markus Friedl, Niels Provos, Theo de Raadt and Dug Song removed many  bugs,
     re-added  newer  features  and  created OpenSSH.  Markus Friedl contributed the support for SSH
     protocol versions 1.5 and 2.0.

4mSSH_CONFIG24m(5)                            File Formats Manual                           4mSSH_CONFIG24m(5)

1mNAME0m
     1mssh_config 22m—— OpenSSH client configuration file

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; obtains configuration data from the following sources in the following order:

           1.   command-line options
           2.   user's configuration file (4m~/.ssh/config24m)
           3.   system-wide configuration file (4m/etc/ssh/ssh_config24m)

     Unless  noted  otherwise,  for  each configuration directive, the first specified value will be
     used.

     The configuration files may contain sections separated by conditional 1mHost 22mor 1mMatch 22mdirectives.
     Configuration in these sections is only applied if the conditional directive that  started  the
     section matches.

     Since  the  first  obtained  value  for each directive is used, more host-specific declarations
     should be given near the beginning of the file, and general defaults at the end.

     The file contains directive/values pairs, one per line.  Lines  starting  with  ‘#’  and  empty
     lines are interpreted as comments.  ‘#’ outside of a quoted string may be used to add a comment
     to  the end of a line.  Whitespace at the beginning or end of lines is ignored.  Values may op‐
     tionally be enclosed in double quotes (") in order to represent arguments containing spaces.

     Configuration directives are separated from their values by whitespace or exactly one ‘=’ char‐
     acter (which may be surrounded by whitespace); the latter format is useful to avoid the need to
     quote whitespace when specifying configuration options using the 1mssh22m, 1mscp22m, and 1msftp -o 22moption.

     The possible keywords and their meanings are as follows (note that keywords  are  case-insensi‐
     tive and arguments are case-sensitive):

     1mHost    22mRestricts  the following declarations (up to the next 1mHost 22mor 1mMatch 22mkeyword) to be only
             for those hosts that match one of the patterns given after the keyword.  If  more  than
             one  pattern  is  provided,  they should be separated by whitespace.  A single ‘*’ as a
             pattern can be used to provide global defaults for all hosts.  The host is usually  the
             4mhostname24m  argument  given on the command line (see the 1mCanonicalizeHostname 22mkeyword for
             exceptions).

             A pattern entry may be negated by prefixing it with an exclamation mark  (‘!’).   If  a
             negated  entry  is  matched,  then the 1mHost 22mentry is ignored, regardless of whether any
             other patterns on the line match.  Negated matches are therefore useful to provide  ex‐
             ceptions for wildcard matches.

             See “PATTERNS” for more information on patterns.

     1mMatch   22mRestricts  the following declarations (up to the next 1mHost 22mor 1mMatch 22mkeyword) to be used
             only when the conditions following the 1mMatch 22mkeyword are satisfied.   Match  conditions
             are  specified using one or more criteria or the single token 1mall 22mwhich always matches.
             The available criteria  keywords  are:  1mcanonical22m,  1mfinal22m,  1mexec22m,  1mlocalnetwork22m,  1mhost22m,
             1moriginalhost22m, 1mtagged22m, 1mcommand22m, 1muser22m, 1mlocaluser22m, and 1mversion22m.  The 1mall 22mcriteria must ap‐
             pear alone or immediately after 1mcanonical 22mor 1mfinal22m.  Other criteria may be combined ar‐
             bitrarily.   All  criteria but 1mall22m, 1mcanonical22m, and 1mfinal 22mrequire an argument.  Criteria
             may be negated by prepending an exclamation mark (‘!’).

             The 1mcanonical 22mkeyword matches only when the configuration file is being re-parsed after
             hostname canonicalization (see the 1mCanonicalizeHostname 22moption).  This may be useful to
             specify conditions that work with canonical host names only.

             The 1mfinal 22mkeyword requests that the configuration be re-parsed (regardless  of  whether
             1mCanonicalizeHostname  22mis  enabled),  and  matches  only  during  this  final  pass.  If
             1mCanonicalizeHostname 22mis enabled, then 1mcanonical 22mand 1mfinal 22mmatch during the same pass.

             The 1mexec 22mkeyword executes the specified command under the user's shell.  If the command
             returns a zero exit status then the condition is considered true.  Commands  containing
             whitespace characters must be quoted.  Arguments to 1mexec 22maccept the tokens described in
             the “TOKENS” section.

             The  1mlocalnetwork  22mkeyword  matches  the  addresses  of active local network interfaces
             against the supplied list of networks in CIDR format.  This may be convenient for vary‐
             ing the effective configuration on devices that roam between networks.  Note that  net‐
             work address is not a trustworthy criteria in many situations (e.g. when the network is
             automatically  configured  using  DHCP) and so caution should be applied if using it to
             control security-sensitive configuration.

             The other keywords' criteria must be single entries or comma-separated  lists  and  may
             use the wildcard and negation operators described in the “PATTERNS” section.

             The  criteria  for  the 1mhost 22mkeyword are matched against the target hostname, after any
             substitution by the 1mHostname 22mor 1mCanonicalizeHostname 22moptions.  The 1moriginalhost 22mkeyword
             matches against the hostname as it was specified on the command-line.

             The 1mtagged 22mkeyword matches a tag name specified by a prior  1mTag  22mdirective  or  on  the
             8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  command-line using the 1m-P 22mflag.  The 1mcommand 22mkeyword matches the remote command
             that has been requested, or the subsystem name that is being invoked (e.g.  "sftp"  for
             an  SFTP session).  The empty string will match the case where a command or tag has not
             been specified, i.e. ‘Match tag ""’.  The 1mversion 22mkeyword matches against  the  version
             string of 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;, for example “OpenSSH_10.0”.

             The 1muser 22mkeyword matches against the target username on the remote host.  The 1mlocaluser0m
             keyword  matches against the name of the local user running 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; (this keyword may be
             useful in system-wide 1mssh_config 22mfiles).

             Finally, the 1msessiontype 22mkeyword matches the requested session type, which may  be  one
             of  1mshell  22mfor interactive sessions, 1mexec 22mfor command execution sessions, 1msubsystem 22mfor
             subsystem invocations such as 8;;man:sftp(1)4msftp24m(1)8;;, or 1mnone 22mfor  transport-only  sessions,  such  as
             when 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; is started with the 1m-N 22mflag.

     1mInclude0m
             Include  the  specified configuration file(s).  Multiple pathnames may be specified and
             each pathname may contain 8;;man:glob(7)4mglob24m(7)8;; wildcards, tokens as described in the  “TOKENS”  sec‐
             tion,  environment  variables  as described in the “ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES” section and,
             for user configurations, shell-like ‘~’ references to user home directories.  Wildcards
             will be expanded and processed in lexical order.  Files without absolute paths are  as‐
             sumed  to be in 4m~/.ssh24m if included in a user configuration file or 4m/etc/ssh24m if included
             from the system configuration file.  1mInclude 22mdirective may appear  inside  a  1mMatch  22mor
             1mHost 22mblock to perform conditional inclusion.

     1mAddKeysToAgent0m
             Specifies  whether  keys  should  be automatically added to a running 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;.  If
             this option is set to 1myes 22mand a key is loaded from a file, the key and  its  passphrase
             are  added to the agent with the default lifetime, as if by 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;;.  If this option
             is set to 1mask22m, 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will require confirmation using the  4mSSH_ASKPASS24m  program  before
             adding  a key (see 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;; for details).  If this option is set to 1mconfirm22m, each use
             of the key must be confirmed, as if the 1m-c 22moption was specified to 8;;man:ssh-add(1)4mssh-add24m(1)8;;.  If this
             option is set to 1mno22m, no keys are added to the agent.  Alternately, this option  may  be
             specified  as  a time interval using the format described in the “TIME FORMATS” section
             of 8;;man:sshd_config(5)4msshd_config24m(5)8;; to specify the key's lifetime in 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;, after  which  it  will
             automatically be removed.  The argument must be 1mno 22m(the default), 1myes22m, 1mconfirm 22m(option‐
             ally followed by a time interval), 1mask 22mor a time interval.

     1mAddressFamily0m
             Specifies  which  address  family to use when connecting.  Valid arguments are 1many 22m(the
             default), 1minet 22m(use IPv4 only), or 1minet6 22m(use IPv6 only).

     1mBatchMode0m
             If set to 1myes22m, user interaction such as password prompts and host key confirmation  re‐
             quests  will  be disabled.  This option is useful in scripts and other batch jobs where
             no user is present to interact with 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;.  The argument must be 1myes 22mor  1mno  22m(the  de‐
             fault).

     1mBindAddress0m
             Use the specified address on the local machine as the source address of the connection.
             Only useful on systems with more than one address.

     1mBindInterface0m
             Use  the  address of the specified interface on the local machine as the source address
             of the connection.

     1mCanonicalDomains0m
             When 1mCanonicalizeHostname 22mis enabled, this option specifies the list of domain suffixes
             in which to search for the specified destination host.

     1mCanonicalizeFallbackLocal0m
             Specifies whether to fail with an error when hostname canonicalization fails.  The  de‐
             fault,  1myes22m,  will  attempt  to  look  up the unqualified hostname using the system re‐
             solver's search rules.   A  value  of  1mno  22mwill  cause  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  to  fail  instantly  if
             1mCanonicalizeHostname  22mis  enabled and the target hostname cannot be found in any of the
             domains specified by 1mCanonicalDomains22m.

     1mCanonicalizeHostname0m
             Controls whether explicit hostname canonicalization is performed.  The default, 1mno22m,  is
             not  to  perform  any  name  rewriting  and let the system resolver handle all hostname
             lookups.  If set to 1myes 22mthen, for  connections  that  do  not  use  a  1mProxyCommand  22mor
             1mProxyJump22m,  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  will  attempt to canonicalize the hostname specified on the command
             line using the 1mCanonicalDomains 22msuffixes  and  1mCanonicalizePermittedCNAMEs  22mrules.   If
             1mCanonicalizeHostname 22mis set to 1malways22m, then canonicalization is applied to proxied con‐
             nections too.

             If  this  option is enabled, then the configuration files are processed again using the
             new target name to pick up any new configuration in matching 1mHost 22mand 1mMatch 22mstanzas.  A
             value of 1mnone 22mdisables the use of a 1mProxyJump 22mhost.

     1mCanonicalizeMaxDots0m
             Specifies the maximum number of dot characters in a hostname before canonicalization is
             disabled.  The default, 1, allows a single dot (i.e. hostname.subdomain).

     1mCanonicalizePermittedCNAMEs0m
             Specifies rules to determine whether CNAMEs  should  be  followed  when  canonicalizing
             hostnames.      The     rules     consist    of    one    or    more    arguments    of
             4msource_domain_list24m:4mtarget_domain_list24m, where 4msource_domain_list24m is  a  pattern-list  of
             domains  that  may  follow CNAMEs in canonicalization, and 4mtarget_domain_list24m is a pat‐
             tern-list of domains that they may resolve to.

             For example,  "*.a.example.com:*.b.example.com,*.c.example.com"  will  allow  hostnames
             matching  "*.a.example.com"  to  be  canonicalized to names in the "*.b.example.com" or
             "*.c.example.com" domains.

             A single argument of "none" causes no CNAMEs to  be  considered  for  canonicalization.
             This is the default behaviour.

     1mCASignatureAlgorithms0m
             Specifies  which  algorithms are allowed for signing of certificates by certificate au‐
             thorities (CAs).  The default is:

                   ssh-ed25519,ecdsa-sha2-nistp256,
                   ecdsa-sha2-nistp384,ecdsa-sha2-nistp521,
                   sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,
                   sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                   rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256,
                   ssh-mldsa44-ed25519

             If the specified list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified  algorithms  will
             be appended to the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins
             with  a  ‘-’ character, then the specified algorithms (including wildcards) will be re‐
             moved from the default set instead of replacing them.

             8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will not accept host certificates signed using algorithms other than those spec‐
             ified.

     1mCertificateFile0m
             Specifies a file from which the user's certificate is read.   A  corresponding  private
             key  must  be  provided  separately  in  order  to  use this certificate either from an
             1mIdentityFile 22mdirective or 1m-i 22mflag to 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;, via 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;, or via a  1mPKCS11Provider0m
             or 1mSecurityKeyProvider22m.

             Arguments  to 1mCertificateFile 22mmay use the tilde syntax to refer to a user's home direc‐
             tory, the tokens described in the “TOKENS” section and  environment  variables  as  de‐
             scribed in the “ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES” section.

             It  is  possible  to  have multiple certificate files specified in configuration files;
             these certificates will be tried in sequence.  Multiple 1mCertificateFile 22mdirectives will
             add to the list of certificates used for authentication.

     1mChannelTimeout0m
             Specifies whether and how quickly 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; should close inactive channels.  Timeouts  are
             specified  as  one  or  more  “type=interval”  pairs separated by whitespace, where the
             “type” must be the special keyword “global” or a channel type name from the list below,
             optionally containing wildcard characters.

             The timeout value “interval” is specified in seconds or may use any of the units  docu‐
             mented  in  the “TIME FORMATS” section.  For example, “session=5m” would cause interac‐
             tive sessions to terminate after five minutes of inactivity.  Specifying a  zero  value
             disables the inactivity timeout.

             The  special  timeout “global” applies to all active channels, taken together.  Traffic
             on any active channel will reset the timeout, but when the  timeout  expires  then  all
             open  channels  will  be closed.  Note that this global timeout is not matched by wild‐
             cards and must be specified explicitly.

             The available channel type names include:

             1magent-connection0m
                     Open connections to 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;.

             1mdirect-tcpip22m, 1mdirect-streamlocal@openssh.com0m
                     Open TCP or Unix socket (respectively) connections that have  been  established
                     from an 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; local forwarding, i.e. 1mLocalForward 22mor 1mDynamicForward22m.

             1mforwarded-tcpip22m, 1mforwarded-streamlocal@openssh.com0m
                     Open  TCP  or Unix socket (respectively) connections that have been established
                     to an 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  listening  on  behalf  of  an  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  remote  forwarding,  i.e.
                     1mRemoteForward22m.

             1msession0m
                     The  interactive  main  session,  including  shell  session, command execution,
                     8;;man:scp(1)4mscp24m(1)8;;, 8;;man:sftp(1)4msftp24m(1)8;;, etc.

             1mtun-connection0m
                     Open 1mTunnelForward 22mconnections.

             1mx11-connection0m
                     Open X11 forwarding sessions.

             Note that in all the above cases, terminating an inactive session does not guarantee to
             remove all resources associated with the session, e.g. shell processes or  X11  clients
             relating to the session may continue to execute.

             Moreover, terminating an inactive channel or session does not necessarily close the SSH
             connection,  nor  does  it prevent a client from requesting another channel of the same
             type.  In particular, expiring an inactive forwarding session does not prevent  another
             identical forwarding from being subsequently created.

             The default is not to expire channels of any type for inactivity.

     1mCheckHostIP0m
             If  set  to  1myes22m, 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will additionally check the host IP address in the 4mknown_hosts0m
             file.  This allows it to detect if a host key changed due to DNS spoofing and will  add
             addresses  of destination hosts to 4m~/.ssh/known_hosts24m in the process, regardless of the
             setting of 1mStrictHostKeyChecking22m.  If the option is set to 1mno 22m(the default), the  check
             will not be executed.

     1mCiphers0m
             Specifies  the ciphers allowed and their order of preference.  Multiple ciphers must be
             comma-separated.  If the specified list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified
             ciphers will be appended to the default set instead of replacing them.  If  the  speci‐
             fied list begins with a ‘-’ character, then the specified ciphers (including wildcards)
             will  be removed from the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list
             begins with a ‘^’ character, then the specified ciphers will be placed at the  head  of
             the default set.

             The supported ciphers are:

                   3des-cbc
                   aes128-cbc
                   aes192-cbc
                   aes256-cbc
                   aes128-ctr
                   aes192-ctr
                   aes256-ctr
                   aes128-gcm@openssh.com
                   aes256-gcm@openssh.com
                   chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com

             The default is:

                   chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,
                   aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,
                   aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr

             The list of available ciphers may also be obtained using "ssh -Q cipher".

     1mClearAllForwardings0m
             Specifies that all local, remote, and dynamic port forwardings specified in the config‐
             uration  files or on the command line be cleared.  This option is primarily useful when
             used from the 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; command line to clear port forwardings set in configuration files,
             and is automatically set by 8;;man:scp(1)4mscp24m(1)8;; and 8;;man:sftp(1)4msftp24m(1)8;;.  The argument must be 1myes  22mor  1mno  22m(the
             default).

     1mCompression0m
             Specifies whether to use compression.  The argument must be 1myes 22mor 1mno 22m(the default).

             Compression  applies  to  all traffic that flows over the SSH connection.  If untrusted
             traffic (such as an open port-forward)  is  permitted  over  the  connection  alongside
             trusted  traffic,  then  compression  may leak information about session contents.  For
             this reason, it is not recommended to enable compression  for  connections  that  share
             trusted and untrusted traffic.

     1mConnectionAttempts0m
             Specifies  the  number  of tries (one per second) to make before exiting.  The argument
             must be an integer.  This may be useful in scripts if the connection  sometimes  fails.
             The default is 1.

     1mConnectTimeout0m
             Specifies  the  timeout (in seconds) used when connecting to the SSH server, instead of
             using the default system TCP timeout.  This timeout is applied both to establishing the
             connection and to performing the initial SSH protocol handshake and key exchange.

     1mControlMaster0m
             Enables the sharing of multiple sessions over a single network connection.  When set to
             1myes22m, 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will listen for  connections  on  a  control  socket  specified  using  the
             1mControlPath  22margument.   Additional  sessions can connect to this socket using the same
             1mControlPath 22mwith 1mControlMaster 22mset to 1mno 22m(the default).  These  sessions  will  try  to
             reuse  the  master  instance's  network connection rather than initiating new ones, but
             will fall back to connecting normally if the control socket does not exist, or  is  not
             listening.

             Setting  this  to  1mask 22mwill cause 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; to listen for control connections, but require
             confirmation using 8;;man:ssh-askpass(1)4mssh-askpass24m(1)8;;.  If the 1mControlPath 22mcannot be  opened,  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  will
             continue without connecting to a master instance.

             X11  and  8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;; forwarding is supported over these multiplexed connections, how‐
             ever the display and agent forwarded will be the one belonging to the master connection
             i.e. it is not possible to forward multiple displays or agents.

             Two additional options allow for opportunistic multiplexing: try to use a  master  con‐
             nection  but  fall back to creating a new one if one does not already exist.  These op‐
             tions are: 1mauto 22mand 1mautoask22m.  The latter requires confirmation like the 1mask 22moption.

     1mControlPath0m
             Specify the path to the control socket used for connection sharing as described in  the
             1mControlMaster  22msection  above  or the string 1mnone 22mto disable connection sharing.  Argu‐
             ments to 1mControlPath 22mmay use the tilde syntax to refer to a user's home directory,  the
             tokens  described in the “TOKENS” section and environment variables as described in the
             “ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES” section.  It is recommended that any 1mControlPath 22mused  for  op‐
             portunistic  connection  sharing  include at least %h, %p, and %r (or alternatively %C)
             and be placed in a directory that is not writable by other users.   This  ensures  that
             shared connections are uniquely identified.

     1mControlPersist0m
             When  used  in  conjunction  with  1mControlMaster22m,  specifies that the master connection
             should remain open in the background (waiting for future client connections) after  the
             initial client connection has been closed.  If set to 1mno 22m(the default), then the master
             connection  will  not be placed into the background, and will close as soon as the ini‐
             tial client connection is closed.  If set to 1myes 22mor 0, then the master connection  will
             remain  in  the background indefinitely (until killed or closed via a mechanism such as
             the "ssh -O exit").  If set to a time in seconds, or a time in any of the formats docu‐
             mented in 8;;man:sshd_config(5)4msshd_config24m(5)8;;, then the backgrounded master  connection  will  automatically
             terminate  after  it  has  remained idle (with no client connections) for the specified
             time.

     1mDynamicForward0m
             Specifies that a TCP port on the local machine be forwarded over  the  secure  channel,
             and the application protocol is then used to determine where to connect to from the re‐
             mote machine.

             The argument must be [4mbind_address24m:]4mport24m.  IPv6 addresses can be specified by enclosing
             addresses  in  square brackets.  By default, the local port is bound in accordance with
             the 1mGatewayPorts 22msetting.  However, an explicit 4mbind_address24m may be used  to  bind  the
             connection  to  a  specific  address.  The 4mbind_address24m of 1mlocalhost 22mindicates that the
             listening port be bound for local use only, while an empty  address  or  ‘*’  indicates
             that the port should be available from all interfaces.

             Currently the SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 protocols are supported, and 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; will act as a SOCKS
             server.  Multiple forwardings may be specified, and additional forwardings can be given
             on the command line.  Only the superuser can forward privileged ports.

     1mEnableEscapeCommandline0m
             Enables  the  command  line option in the 1mEscapeChar 22mmenu for interactive sessions (de‐
             fault ‘~C’).  By default, the command line is disabled.

     1mEnableSSHKeysign0m
             Setting this option to 1myes 22min the global client configuration file  4m/etc/ssh/ssh_config0m
             enables  the  use  of the helper program 8;;man:ssh-keysign(8)4mssh-keysign24m(8)8;; during 1mHostbasedAuthentication22m.
             The argument must be 1myes 22mor 1mno 22m(the default).  This option should be placed in the non-
             hostspecific section.  See 8;;man:ssh-keysign(8)4mssh-keysign24m(8)8;; for more information.

     1mEscapeChar0m
             Sets the escape character (default: ‘~’).  The escape character can also be set on  the
             command  line.  The argument should be a single character, ‘^’ followed by a letter, or
             1mnone 22mto disable the escape character entirely (making the  connection  transparent  for
             binary data).

     1mExitOnForwardFailure0m
             Specifies  whether  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  should terminate the connection if it cannot set up all re‐
             quested dynamic, tunnel, local, and remote port forwardings, (e.g. if either end is un‐
             able to bind and listen on a specified port).  Note that 1mExitOnForwardFailure 22mdoes  not
             apply to connections made over port forwardings and will not, for example, cause 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;
             to  exit  if TCP connections to the ultimate forwarding destination fail.  The argument
             must be 1myes 22mor 1mno 22m(the default).

     1mFingerprintHash0m
             Specifies the hash algorithm used when displaying key fingerprints.  Valid options are:
             1mmd5 22mand 1msha256 22m(the default).

     1mForkAfterAuthentication0m
             Requests 1mssh 22mto go to background just before command execution.  This is useful if  1mssh0m
             is  going to ask for passwords or passphrases, but the user wants it in the background.
             This implies the 1mStdinNull 22mconfiguration option being set to  “yes”.   The  recommended
             way  to  start  X11 programs at a remote site is with something like 1mssh -f host xterm22m,
             which is the same as 1mssh host xterm 22mif the 1mForkAfterAuthentication 22mconfiguration option
             is set to “yes”.

             If the 1mExitOnForwardFailure 22mconfiguration option is set to “yes”, then a client started
             with the 1mForkAfterAuthentication 22mconfiguration option being set to “yes” will wait  for
             all  remote  port  forwards to be successfully established before placing itself in the
             background.  The argument to this keyword must be 1myes 22m(same as the  1m-f  22moption)  or  1mno0m
             (the default).

     1mForwardAgent0m
             Specifies whether the connection to the authentication agent (if any) will be forwarded
             to  the remote machine.  The argument may be 1myes22m, 1mno 22m(the default), an explicit path to
             an agent socket or the name of an environment variable (beginning with ‘$’) in which to
             find the path.

             Agent forwarding should be enabled with caution.  Users with the ability to bypass file
             permissions on the remote host (for the agent's Unix-domain socket) can access the  lo‐
             cal  agent  through  the  forwarded connection.  An attacker cannot obtain key material
             from the agent, however they can perform operations on the keys that enable them to au‐
             thenticate using the identities loaded into the agent.

     1mForwardX110m
             Specifies whether X11 connections will be  automatically  redirected  over  the  secure
             channel and 4mDISPLAY24m set.  The argument must be 1myes 22mor 1mno 22m(the default).

             X11  forwarding  should be enabled with caution.  Users with the ability to bypass file
             permissions on the remote host (for the user's X11 authorization database)  can  access
             the  local  X11 display through the forwarded connection.  An attacker may then be able
