sshd_config.text:
4mSSHD_CONFIG24m(5)                           File Formats Manual                          4mSSHD_CONFIG24m(5)

1mNAME0m
     1msshd_config 22m—— OpenSSH daemon configuration file

1mDESCRIPTION0m
     8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  reads  configuration  data from 4m/etc/ssh/sshd_config24m (or the file specified with 1m-f 22mon
     the command line).  The file contains keyword-argument pairs, one per line.  Unless noted  oth‐
     erwise,  for  each keyword, the first obtained value will be used.  Lines starting with ‘#’ and
     empty lines are interpreted as comments.  Arguments may optionally be enclosed in double quotes
     (") in order to represent arguments containing spaces.

     The possible keywords and their meanings are as follows (note that keywords  are  case-insensi‐
     tive and arguments are case-sensitive):

     1mAcceptEnv0m
             Specifies  what  environment  variables sent by the client will be copied into the ses‐
             sion's 8;;man:environ(7)4menviron24m(7)8;;.  See 1mSendEnv 22mand 1mSetEnv 22min 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for how  to  configure  the
             client.   The 4mTERM24m environment variable is always accepted whenever the client requests
             a pseudo-terminal as it is required by the protocol.  Variables are specified by  name,
             which  may contain the wildcard characters ‘*’ and ‘?’.  Multiple environment variables
             may be separated by whitespace or spread  across  multiple  1mAcceptEnv  22mdirectives.   Be
             warned that some environment variables could be used to bypass restricted user environ‐
             ments.   For  this  reason, care should be taken in the use of this directive.  The de‐
             fault is not to accept any environment variables.

     1mAddressFamily0m
             Specifies which address family should be used by 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;.  Valid arguments are 1many 22m(the
             default), 1minet 22m(use IPv4 only), or 1minet6 22m(use IPv6 only).

     1mAgentSocketPath0m
             Specifies the filesystem path used for forwarded 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;; sockets.  Sockets may  be
             created in either a shared location or a user-specific directory.  User-specific direc‐
             tories  are  specified  by prefixing the path name with 1muser:22m.  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; will ensure the
             directory exists and create the listening socket directly in  it.   Relative  user-spe‐
             cific directory paths will be created relative to the user's $4mHOME24m directory.

             Shared  directories  may  be specified by prefixing an absolute path name with 1mshared:22m.
             In this case, a temporary subdirectory will be created under  the  specified  directory
             and the listening agent socket will be created in that.

             1mAgentSocketPath 22maccepts the tokens described in the “TOKENS” section.  The default path
             specification is 4muser:.ssh/agent24m.

     1mAllowAgentForwarding0m
             Specifies whether 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;; forwarding is permitted.  The default is 1myes22m.  Note that
             disabling agent forwarding does not improve security unless users are also denied shell
             access, as they can always install their own forwarders.

     1mAllowGroups0m
             This keyword can be followed by a list of group name patterns, separated by spaces.  If
             specified,  login  is allowed only for users whose primary group or supplementary group
             list matches one of the patterns.  Only group names are valid; a numerical group ID  is
             not  recognized.  By default, login is allowed for all groups.  1mAllowGroups 22mis not con‐
             sulted for groups matched by 1mDenyGroups22m.

             See PATTERNS in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for more information on patterns.  This keyword  may  ap‐
             pear multiple times in 1msshd_config 22mwith each instance appending to the list.

     1mAllowStreamLocalForwarding0m
             Specifies whether StreamLocal (Unix-domain socket) forwarding is permitted.  The avail‐
             able  options  are 1myes 22m(the default) or 1mall 22mto allow StreamLocal forwarding, 1mno 22mto pre‐
             vent all StreamLocal forwarding, 1mlocal 22mto allow local (from the perspective of  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;)
             forwarding only or 1mremote 22mto allow remote forwarding only.  Note that disabling Stream‐
             Local  forwarding  does not improve security unless users are also denied shell access,
             as they can always install their own forwarders.

     1mAllowTcpForwarding0m
             Specifies whether TCP forwarding is permitted.  The available options are 1myes 22m(the  de‐
             fault) or 1mall 22mto allow TCP forwarding, 1mno 22mto prevent all TCP forwarding, 1mlocal 22mto allow
             local  (from  the perspective of 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;) forwarding only or 1mremote 22mto allow remote for‐
             warding only.  Note that disabling TCP forwarding  does  not  improve  security  unless
             users are also denied shell access, as they can always install their own forwarders.

     1mAllowUsers0m
             This  keyword can be followed by a list of user name patterns, separated by spaces.  If
             specified, login is allowed only for user names that match one of the  patterns.   Only
             user  names are valid; a numerical user ID is not recognized.  By default, login is al‐
             lowed for all users.  If the pattern takes the form USER@HOST then USER  and  HOST  are
             separately checked, restricting logins to particular users from particular hosts.  HOST
             criteria  may  additionally  contain addresses to match in CIDR address/masklen format.
             1mAllowUsers 22mis not consulted for users matched by 1mDenyUsers22m.

             See PATTERNS in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for more information on patterns.  This keyword  may  ap‐
             pear multiple times in 1msshd_config 22mwith each instance appending to the list.

     1mAuthenticationMethods0m
             Specifies  the authentication methods that must be successfully completed for a user to
             be granted access.  This option must be followed by one or more  lists  of  comma-sepa‐
             rated  authentication method names, or by the single string 1many 22mto indicate the default
             behaviour of accepting any single authentication method.  If the default is overridden,
             then successful authentication requires completion of every method in at least  one  of
             these lists.

             For example, "publickey,password publickey,keyboard-interactive" would require the user
             to complete public key authentication, followed by either password or keyboard interac‐
             tive  authentication.   Only  methods that are next in one or more lists are offered at
             each stage, so for this example it would not be possible to attempt  password  or  key‐
             board-interactive authentication before public key.

             For  keyboard interactive authentication it is also possible to restrict authentication
             to a specific device by appending a colon followed by the device identifier 1mbsdauth  22mor
             1mpam22m.       depending     on     the     server     configuration.      For     example,
             "keyboard-interactive:bsdauth" would restrict keyboard  interactive  authentication  to
             the 1mbsdauth 22mdevice.

             If  the publickey method is listed more than once, 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; verifies that keys that have
             been used successfully are not reused for  subsequent  authentications.   For  example,
             "publickey,publickey"  requires  successful  authentication  using two different public
             keys.

             Note that each authentication method listed should also be explicitly  enabled  in  the
             configuration.

             The    available    authentication   methods   are:   "gssapi-with-mic",   "hostbased",
             "keyboard-interactive",  "none"  (used  for  access  to  password-less  accounts   when
             1mPermitEmptyPasswords 22mis enabled), "password" and "publickey".

     1mAuthorizedKeysCommand0m
             Specifies  a program to be used to look up the user's public keys.  The program must be
             owned by root, not writable by group or others and specified by an absolute path.   Ar‐
             guments  to  1mAuthorizedKeysCommand 22maccept the tokens described in the “TOKENS” section.
             If no arguments are specified then the username of the target user is used.

             The program should produce on standard output zero or  more  lines  of  authorized_keys
             output  (see  1mAUTHORIZED_KEYS  22min  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;).   1mAuthorizedKeysCommand 22mis tried after the
             usual 1mAuthorizedKeysFile 22mfiles and will not be executed if  a  matching  key  is  found
             there.  By default, no 1mAuthorizedKeysCommand 22mis run.  This command is only executed for
             valid users.

     1mAuthorizedKeysCommandUser0m
             Specifies  the user under whose account the 1mAuthorizedKeysCommand 22mis run.  It is recom‐
             mended to use a dedicated user that has no other role on the host than  running  autho‐
             rized     keys     commands.      If    1mAuthorizedKeysCommand    22mis    specified    but
             1mAuthorizedKeysCommandUser 22mis not, then 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; will refuse to start.

     1mAuthorizedKeysFile0m
             Specifies the file that contains the public keys used  for  user  authentication.   The
             format  is  described in the AUTHORIZED_KEYS FILE FORMAT section of 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;.  Arguments
             to 1mAuthorizedKeysFile 22mmay include wildcards and accept  the  tokens  described  in  the
             “TOKENS”  section.  After expansion, 1mAuthorizedKeysFile 22mis taken to be an absolute path
             or one relative to the user's home directory.  Multiple files may be listed,  separated
             by  whitespace.   Alternately  this option may be set to 1mnone 22mto skip checking for user
             keys in files.  The default  is  ".ssh/authorized_keys  .ssh/authorized_keys2".   These
             files are only checked for valid users.

     1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand0m
             Specifies  a  program to be used to generate the list of allowed certificate principals
             as per 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile22m.  The program must be owned by root,  not  writable  by
             group    or    others    and   specified   by   an   absolute   path.    Arguments   to
             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand 22maccept the tokens described in the “TOKENS” section.  If no
             arguments are specified then the username of the target user is used.

             The  program  should   produce   on   standard   output   zero   or   more   lines   of
             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile    22moutput.     If    either   1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand   22mor
             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile 22mis specified, then certificates offered by the client for  au‐
             thentication   must   contain   a   principal   that   is   listed.    By  default,  no
             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand 22mis run.  This command is only executed for valid users.

     1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommandUser0m
             Specifies the user under whose account the 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand 22mis run.   It  is
             recommended to use a dedicated user that has no other role on the host than running au‐
             thorized   principals   commands.   If  1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand  22mis  specified  but
             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommandUser 22mis not, then 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; will refuse to start.

     1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile0m
             Specifies a file that lists principal names that are accepted for certificate authenti‐
             cation.  When using certificates signed by a key listed in 1mTrustedUserCAKeys22m, this file
             lists names, one of which must appear in the certificate for it to be accepted for  au‐
             thentication.   Names  are listed one per line preceded by key options (as described in
             1mAUTHORIZED_KEYS FILE FORMAT 22min 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;).  Empty lines and comments  starting  with  ‘#’
             are ignored.

             Arguments  to  1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile 22mmay include wildcards and accept the tokens de‐
             scribed in the “TOKENS” section.  After expansion, 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile 22mis taken to
             be an absolute path or one relative to the user's home directory.  The default is 1mnone22m,
             i.e. not to use a principals file – in this case, the username of the user must  appear
             in  a  certificate's  principals list for it to be accepted.  This file is only checked
             for valid users.

             Note that 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile 22mis only used when authentication proceeds using a CA
             listed in 1mTrustedUserCAKeys 22mand is not consulted for certification authorities  trusted
             via 4m~/.ssh/authorized_keys24m, though the 1mprincipals= 22mkey option offers a similar facility
             (see 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; for details).

     1mBanner  22mThe contents of the specified file are sent to the remote user before authentication is
             allowed.   If  the argument is 1mnone 22mthen no banner is displayed.  By default, no banner
             is displayed.

     1mCASignatureAlgorithms0m
             Specifies which algorithms are allowed for signing of certificates by  certificate  au‐
             thorities (CAs).  The default is:

                   ssh-ed25519,ecdsa-sha2-nistp256,
                   ecdsa-sha2-nistp384,ecdsa-sha2-nistp521,
                   sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,
                   sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                   rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256,
                   ssh-mldsa44-ed25519

             If  the  specified list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified algorithms will
             be appended to the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins
             with a ‘-’ character, then the specified algorithms (including wildcards) will  be  re‐
             moved from the default set instead of replacing them.

             Certificates signed using other algorithms will not be accepted for public key or host-
             based authentication.

     1mChannelTimeout0m
             Specifies whether and how quickly 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; should close inactive channels.  Timeouts are
             specified  as  one  or  more  “type=interval”  pairs separated by whitespace, where the
             “type” must be the special keyword “global” or a channel type name from the list below,
             optionally containing wildcard characters.

             The timeout value “interval” is specified in seconds or may use any of the units  docu‐
             mented  in  the “TIME FORMATS” section.  For example, “session=5m” would cause interac‐
             tive sessions to terminate after five minutes of inactivity.  Specifying a  zero  value
             disables the inactivity timeout.

             The  special  timeout “global” applies to all active channels, taken together.  Traffic
             on any active channel will reset the timeout, but when the  timeout  expires  then  all
             open  channels  will  be closed.  Note that this global timeout is not matched by wild‐
             cards and must be specified explicitly.

             The available channel type names include:

             1magent-connection0m
                     Open connections to 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;.

             1mdirect-tcpip22m, 1mdirect-streamlocal@openssh.com0m
                     Open TCP or Unix socket (respectively) connections that have  been  established
                     from an 8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;; local forwarding, i.e. 1mLocalForward 22mor 1mDynamicForward22m.

             1mforwarded-tcpip22m, 1mforwarded-streamlocal@openssh.com0m
                     Open  TCP  or Unix socket (respectively) connections that have been established
                     to an 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  listening  on  behalf  of  an  8;;man:ssh(1)4mssh24m(1)8;;  remote  forwarding,  i.e.
                     1mRemoteForward22m.

             1msession0m
                     The  interactive  main  session,  including  shell  session, command execution,
                     8;;man:scp(1)4mscp24m(1)8;;, 8;;man:sftp(1)4msftp24m(1)8;;, etc.

             1mtun-connection0m
                     Open 1mTunnelForward 22mconnections.

             1mx11-connection0m
                     Open X11 forwarding sessions.

             Note that in all the above cases, terminating an inactive session does not guarantee to
             remove all resources associated with the session, e.g. shell processes or  X11  clients
             relating to the session may continue to execute.

             Moreover, terminating an inactive channel or session does not necessarily close the SSH
             connection,  nor  does  it prevent a client from requesting another channel of the same
             type.  In particular, expiring an inactive forwarding session does not prevent  another
             identical forwarding from being subsequently created.

             The default is not to expire channels of any type for inactivity.

     1mChrootDirectory0m
             Specifies the pathname of a directory to 8;;man:chroot(2)4mchroot24m(2)8;; to after authentication.  At session
             startup  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  checks that all components of the pathname are root-owned directories
             which are not writable by group or others.  After the chroot, 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; changes the work‐
             ing directory to the user's home directory.  Arguments to  1mChrootDirectory  22maccept  the
             tokens described in the “TOKENS” section.

             The  1mChrootDirectory  22mmust  contain  the necessary files and directories to support the
             user's session.  For an interactive session this requires at least a  shell,  typically
             8;;man:sh(1)4msh24m(1)8;;,  and  basic 4m/dev24m nodes such as 8;;man:null(4)4mnull24m(4)8;;, 8;;man:zero(4)4mzero24m(4)8;;, 8;;man:stdin(4)4mstdin24m(4)8;;, 8;;man:stdout(4)4mstdout24m(4)8;;, 8;;man:stderr(4)4mstderr24m(4)8;;,
             and 8;;man:tty(4)4mtty24m(4)8;; devices.  For file transfer sessions using SFTP no additional  configuration
             of  the environment is necessary if the in-process sftp-server is used, though sessions
             which use logging may require 4m/dev/log24m inside the chroot directory  on  some  operating
             systems (see 8;;man:sftp-server(8)4msftp-server24m(8)8;; for details).

             For safety, it is very important that the directory hierarchy be prevented from modifi‐
             cation  by  other processes on the system (especially those outside the jail).  Miscon‐
             figuration can lead to unsafe environments which 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; cannot detect.

             The default is 1mnone22m, indicating not to 8;;man:chroot(2)4mchroot24m(2)8;;.

     1mCiphers0m
             Specifies the ciphers allowed.  Multiple ciphers must be comma-separated.  If the spec‐
             ified list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified ciphers will be appended  to
             the  default  set  instead  of replacing them.  If the specified list begins with a ‘-’
             character, then the specified ciphers (including wildcards) will be  removed  from  the
             default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins with a ‘^’ charac‐
             ter, then the specified ciphers will be placed at the head of the default set.

             The supported ciphers are:

                   3des-cbc
                   aes128-cbc
                   aes192-cbc
                   aes256-cbc
                   aes128-ctr
                   aes192-ctr
                   aes256-ctr
                   aes128-gcm@openssh.com
                   aes256-gcm@openssh.com
                   chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com

             The default is:

                   chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,
                   aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,
                   aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-ctr

             The list of available ciphers may also be obtained using "ssh -Q cipher".

     1mClientAliveCountMax0m
             Sets  the  number  of client alive messages which may be sent without 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; receiving
             any messages back from the client.  If this threshold is  reached  while  client  alive
             messages  are being sent, sshd will disconnect the client, terminating the session.  It
             is important to note that the use of client  alive  messages  is  very  different  from
             1mTCPKeepAlive22m.   The  client  alive  messages are sent through the encrypted channel and
             therefore will not be spoofable.  The TCP keepalive option enabled by  1mTCPKeepAlive  22mis
             spoofable.   The client alive mechanism is valuable when the client or server depend on
             knowing when a connection has become unresponsive.

             The default value is 3.  If 1mClientAliveInterval 22mis set to 15,  and  1mClientAliveCountMax0m
             is  left  at  the default, unresponsive SSH clients will be disconnected after approxi‐
             mately 45 seconds.  Setting a zero 1mClientAliveCountMax 22mdisables connection termination.

     1mClientAliveInterval0m
             Sets a timeout interval in seconds after which if no data has been  received  from  the
             client, 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; will send a message through the encrypted channel to request a response
             from  the client.  The default is 0, indicating that these messages will not be sent to
             the client.

     1mCompression0m
             Specifies whether compression is enabled after the user has authenticated successfully.
             The argument must be 1myes22m, 1mdelayed 22m(a legacy synonym for 1myes22m), or 1mno22m.   The  default  is
             1myes22m.

             Compression  applies  to  all traffic that flows over the SSH connection.  If untrusted
             traffic (such as an open port-forward)  is  permitted  over  the  connection  alongside
             trusted  traffic,  then  compression  may leak information about session contents.  For
             this reason, it is not recommended to enable compression  for  connections  that  share
             trusted and untrusted traffic.

     1mDenyGroups0m
             This  keyword  can  be  followed by a list of group name patterns, separated by spaces.
             Login is disallowed for users whose primary group or supplementary group  list  matches
             one  of  the  patterns.  Only group names are valid; a numerical group ID is not recog‐
             nized.  By default, login is allowed for all groups.  1mAllowGroups 22mis not consulted  for
             groups matched by 1mDenyGroups22m.

             See  PATTERNS  in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for more information on patterns.  This keyword may ap‐
             pear multiple times in 1msshd_config 22mwith each instance appending to the list.

     1mDenyUsers0m
             This keyword can be followed by a list of user name patterns, separated by spaces.  Lo‐
             gin is disallowed for user names that match one of the patterns.  Only user  names  are
             valid;  a  numerical  user  ID is not recognized.  By default, login is allowed for all
             users.  If the pattern takes the form USER@HOST  then  USER  and  HOST  are  separately
             checked,  restricting  logins to particular users from particular hosts.  HOST criteria
             may additionally contain addresses to match in CIDR address/masklen format.  1mAllowUsers0m
             is not consulted for users matched by 1mDenyUsers22m.

             See PATTERNS in 8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_config24m(5)8;; for more information on patterns.  This keyword  may  ap‐
             pear multiple times in 1msshd_config 22mwith each instance appending to the list.

     1mDisableForwarding0m
             Disables  all  forwarding  features,  including X11, 8;;man:ssh-agent(1)4mssh-agent24m(1)8;;, TCP and StreamLocal.
             This option overrides all other forwarding-related options and may simplify  restricted
             configurations.

     1mExposeAuthInfo0m
             Writes  a temporary file containing a list of authentication methods and public creden‐
             tials (e.g. keys) used to authenticate the user.  The location of the file  is  exposed
             to the user session through the 4mSSH_USER_AUTH24m environment variable.  The default is 1mno22m.

     1mFingerprintHash0m
             Specifies  the  hash  algorithm used when logging key fingerprints.  Valid options are:
             1mmd5 22mand 1msha25622m.  The default is 1msha25622m.

     1mForceCommand0m
             Forces the execution of the command specified by  1mForceCommand22m,  ignoring  any  command
             supplied  by  the client and 4m~/.ssh/rc24m if present.  The command is invoked by using the
             user's login shell with the -c option.  This applies to shell,  command,  or  subsystem
             execution.  It is most useful inside a 1mMatch 22mblock.  The command originally supplied by
             the client is available in the 4mSSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND24m environment variable.  Specifying a
             command  of 1minternal-sftp 22mwill force the use of an in-process SFTP server that requires
             no support files when used with 1mChrootDirectory22m.  The default is 1mnone22m.

             This directive does not limit other kinds of access that a client may request via their
             connection, such as TCP, agent, socket or X11 forwarding.  If these  are  not  desired,
             then they must be explicitly disabled, either individually via their respective options
             or all together using the 1mDisableForwarding 22moption.

     1mGatewayPorts0m
             Specifies  whether  remote  hosts  are  allowed  to  connect to ports forwarded for the
             client.  By default, 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; binds remote port forwardings  to  the  loopback  address.
             This  prevents other remote hosts from connecting to forwarded ports.  1mGatewayPorts 22mcan
             be used to specify that sshd should allow remote port forwardings to bind to  non-loop‐
             back  addresses, thus allowing other hosts to connect.  The argument may be 1mno 22mto force
             remote port forwardings to be available to the local host only,  1myes  22mto  force  remote
             port  forwardings  to  bind  to  the  wildcard address, or 1mclientspecified 22mto allow the
             client to select the address to which the forwarding is bound.  The default is 1mno22m.

     1mGSSAPIAuthentication0m
             Specifies whether user authentication based on GSSAPI is allowed.  The default is 1mno22m.

     1mGSSAPICleanupCredentials0m
             Specifies whether to automatically destroy the user's credentials cache on logout.  The
             default is 1myes22m.

     1mGSSAPIDelegateCredentials0m
             Accept delegated credentials on the server side.  The default is 1myes22m.

     1mGSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck0m
             Determines whether to be strict about the identity of the GSSAPI acceptor a client  au‐
             thenticates  against.  If set to 1myes 22mthen the client must authenticate against the host
             service on the current hostname.  If set to 1mno 22mthen the client may authenticate against
             any service key stored in the machine's default store.  This facility  is  provided  to
             assist  with  operation  on multi homed machines.  The default is 1myes22m.  This option may
             not be effective in Windows Active Directory environments.

     1mHostbasedAcceptedAlgorithms0m
             Specifies the signature algorithms that will be accepted for  hostbased  authentication
             as a list of comma-separated patterns.  Alternately if the specified list begins with a
             ‘+’  character, then the specified signature algorithms will be appended to the default
             set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins with a ‘-’ character, then
             the specified signature algorithms (including wildcards) will be removed from  the  de‐
             fault  set  instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins with a ‘^’ charac‐
             ter, then the specified signature algorithms will be placed at the head of the  default
             set.  The default for this option is:

                ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp384-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp521-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                sk-ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                webauthn-sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-512-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ssh-mldsa44-ed25519-cert,
                ssh-ed25519,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp256,ecdsa-sha2-nistp384,ecdsa-sha2-nistp521,
                sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,
                sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                webauthn-sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256,
                ssh-mldsa44-ed2551

             The  list  of  available  signature  algorithms  may  also  be  obtained  using "ssh -Q
             HostbasedAcceptedAlgorithms".  This was formerly named HostbasedAcceptedKeyTypes.

     1mHostbasedAuthentication0m
             Specifies whether rhosts or /etc/hosts.equiv authentication  together  with  successful
             public  key client host authentication is allowed (host-based authentication).  The de‐
             fault is 1mno22m.

             Specifies whether or not the server will attempt to perform a reverse name lookup  when

             The default is 1mno22m.

             must match a private host key already specified by 1mHostKey22m.  The default  behaviour  of
             8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; is not to load any certificates.

             Specifies  a  file  containing  a  private  host  key  used  by  SSH.  The defaults are

             4m/etc/ssh/ssh_host_mldsa44_ed25519_key24m, and 4m/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key24m.

             Note  that  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  will refuse to use a file if it is group/world-accessible and that
             the 1mHostKeyAlgorithms 22moption restricts which of the keys are actually used by 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;.

             Identifies the UNIX-domain socket used to communicate with an agent that has access  to
             the private host keys.  If the string "SSH_AUTH_SOCK" is specified, the location of the
             socket will be read from the 4mSSH_AUTH_SOCK24m environment variable.

     1mHostKeyAlgorithms0m
             Specifies  the  host  key signature algorithms that the server offers.  The default for
             this option is:

                ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp384-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp521-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                sk-ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                webauthn-sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-512-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-256-cert-v01@openssh.com,
                ssh-mldsa44-ed25519-cert,
                ssh-ed25519,
                ecdsa-sha2-nistp256,ecdsa-sha2-nistp384,ecdsa-sha2-nistp521,
                sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,
                sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                webauthn-sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com,
                rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256,
                ssh-mldsa44-ed25519

             The list of  available  signature  algorithms  may  also  be  obtained  using  "ssh  -Q
             HostKeyAlgorithms".

     1mIgnoreRhosts0m
             Specifies   whether   to   ignore   per-user   4m.rhosts24m   and   4m.shosts24m   files   during
             1mHostbasedAuthentication22m.  The system-wide  4m/etc/hosts.equiv24m  and  4m/etc/ssh/shosts.equiv0m
             are still used regardless of this setting.

             Accepted  values are 1myes 22m(the default) to ignore all per-user files, 1mshosts-only 22mto al‐
             low the use of 4m.shosts24m but to ignore 4m.rhosts24m or 1mno 22mto allow both 4m.shosts24m and 4mrhosts24m.

     1mIgnoreUserKnownHosts0m
             Specifies  whether  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;  should  ignore  the   user's   4m~/.ssh/known_hosts24m   during
             1mHostbasedAuthentication    22mand    use   only   the   system-wide   known   hosts   file
             4m/etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts24m.  The default is “no”.

     1mInclude0m
             Include the specified configuration file(s).  Multiple pathnames may be  specified  and
             each pathname may contain 8;;man:glob(7)4mglob24m(7)8;; wildcards that will be expanded and processed in lex‐
             ical  order.   Files  without absolute paths are assumed to be in 4m/etc/ssh24m.  An 1mInclude0m
             directive may appear inside a 1mMatch 22mblock to perform conditional inclusion.

     1mIPQoS   22mSpecifies the 4mDifferentiated24m 4mServices24m 4mField24m 4mCodepoint24m (DSCP) value for the  connection.
             Accepted  values  are 1maf1122m, 1maf1222m, 1maf1322m, 1maf2122m, 1maf2222m, 1maf2322m, 1maf3122m, 1maf3222m, 1maf3322m, 1maf4122m, 1maf4222m,
             1maf4322m, 1mcs022m, 1mcs122m, 1mcs222m, 1mcs322m, 1mcs422m, 1mcs522m, 1mcs622m, 1mcs722m, 1mef22m, 1mle22m, a numeric value, or 1mnone  22mto  use
             the  operating system default.  This option may take one or two arguments, separated by
             whitespace.  If one argument is specified, it is used as the packet class  uncondition‐
             ally.  If two values are specified, the first is automatically selected for interactive
             sessions  and  the  second  for non-interactive sessions.  The default is 1mef 22m(Expedited
             Forwarding) for interactive sessions and 1mnone 22m(the operating system default)  for  non-
             interactive sessions.

     1mKbdInteractiveAuthentication0m
             Specifies  whether  to  allow  keyboard-interactive authentication.  All authentication
             styles from 8;;man:login.conf(5)4mlogin.conf24m(5)8;; are supported.  The default is 1myes22m.   The  argument  to  this
             keyword  must  be 1myes 22mor 1mno22m.  1mChallengeResponseAuthentication 22mis a deprecated alias for
             this.

     1mKerberosAuthentication0m
             Specifies whether the password provided by the user for 1mPasswordAuthentication 22mwill  be
             validated  through  the  Kerberos KDC.  To use this option, the server needs a Kerberos
             servtab which allows the verification of the KDC's identity.  The default is 1mno22m.

     1mKerberosGetAFSToken0m
             If AFS is active and the user has a Kerberos 5 TGT, attempt to acquire an AFS token be‐
             fore accessing the user's home directory.  The default is 1mno22m.

     1mKerberosOrLocalPasswd0m
             If password authentication through Kerberos fails then the password will  be  validated
             via any additional local mechanism such as 4m/etc/passwd24m.  The default is 1myes22m.

     1mKerberosTicketCleanup0m
             Specifies whether to automatically destroy the user's ticket cache file on logout.  The
             default is 1myes22m.

     1mKexAlgorithms0m
             Specifies  the  permitted  KEX  (Key Exchange) algorithms that the server will offer to
             clients.  The ordering of this list is not important, as the client specifies the pref‐
             erence order.  Multiple algorithms must be comma-separated.

             If the specified list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified  algorithms  will
             be appended to the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list begins
             with  a  ‘-’ character, then the specified algorithms (including wildcards) will be re‐
             moved from the default set instead of replacing them.  If  the  specified  list  begins
             with  a  ‘^’ character, then the specified algorithms will be placed at the head of the
             default set.

             The supported algorithms are:

                   curve25519-sha256
                   curve25519-sha256@libssh.org
                   diffie-hellman-group1-sha1
                   diffie-hellman-group14-sha1
                   diffie-hellman-group14-sha256
                   diffie-hellman-group16-sha512
                   diffie-hellman-group18-sha512
                   diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1
                   diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256
                   ecdh-sha2-nistp256
                   ecdh-sha2-nistp384
                   ecdh-sha2-nistp521
                   mlkem768nistp256-sha256
                   mlkem768x25519-sha256
                   sntrup761x25519-sha512
                   sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com

             The default is:

                   mlkem768x25519-sha256,
                   sntrup761x25519-sha512,sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com,
                   curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org,
                   ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521

             The list of supported key exchange algorithms  may  also  be  obtained  using  "ssh  -Q
             KexAlgorithms".

     1mListenAddress0m
             Specifies  the  local  addresses  8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; should listen on.  The following forms may be
             used:

                   1mListenAddress 4m22mhostname24m|4maddress24m [1mrdomain 4m22mdomain24m]
                   1mListenAddress 4m22mhostname24m:4mport24m [1mrdomain 4m22mdomain24m]
                   1mListenAddress 4m22mIPv4_address24m:4mport24m [1mrdomain 4m22mdomain24m]
                   1mListenAddress 22m[4mhostname24m|4maddress24m]:4mport24m [1mrdomain 4m22mdomain24m]

             The optional 1mrdomain 22mqualifier requests 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; listen in an explicit  routing  domain.
             If  4mport24m  is not specified, sshd will listen on the address and all 1mPort 22moptions speci‐
             fied.  The default is to listen on all local addresses on the current  default  routing
             domain.  Multiple 1mListenAddress 22moptions are permitted.  For more information on routing
             domains, see 8;;man:rdomain(4)4mrdomain24m(4)8;;.

     1mLoginGraceTime0m
             The  server disconnects after this time if the user has not successfully logged in.  If
             the value is 0, there is no time limit.  The default is 120 seconds.

     1mLogLevel0m
             Gives the verbosity level that is used when logging messages from 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;.  The  possi‐
             ble  values are: QUIET, FATAL, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, DEBUG1, DEBUG2, and DEBUG3.
             The default is INFO.  DEBUG and DEBUG1 are equivalent.  DEBUG2 and DEBUG3 each  specify
             higher  levels of debugging output.  Logging with a DEBUG level violates the privacy of
             users and is not recommended.

     1mLogVerbose0m
             Specify one or more overrides to 1mLogLevel22m.  An override consists of one or more pattern
             lists that matches the source file, function and line number to force detailed  logging
             for.  For example, an override pattern of:

                   kex.c:*:1000,*:kex_exchange_identification():*,packet.c:*

             would  enable  detailed  logging  for  line  1000  of  4mkex.c24m, everything in the 1mkex_ex‐0m
             1mchange_identification22m() function, and all code in the 4mpacket.c24m file.   This  option  is
             intended for debugging and no overrides are enabled by default.

     1mMACs    22mSpecifies  the  available  MAC (message authentication code) algorithms.  The MAC algo‐
             rithm is used for data integrity protection.  Multiple algorithms must  be  comma-sepa‐
             rated.   If  the  specified  list begins with a ‘+’ character, then the specified algo‐
             rithms will be appended to the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified
             list begins with a ‘-’ character, then the specified algorithms  (including  wildcards)
             will  be removed from the default set instead of replacing them.  If the specified list
             begins with a ‘^’ character, then the specified algorithms will be placed at  the  head
             of the default set.

                   hmac-md5
                   hmac-md5-96
                   hmac-sha1
                   hmac-sha1-96
                   hmac-sha2-256
                   hmac-sha2-512
                   umac-64@openssh.com
                   umac-128@openssh.com
                   hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com
                   hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com
                   hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com
                   hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com
                   hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com
                   hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com
                   umac-64-etm@openssh.com
                   umac-128-etm@openssh.com

             The default is:

                   umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com,
                   hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,
                   hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com,
                   umac-64@openssh.com,umac-128@openssh.com,
                   hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha1

             The list of available MAC algorithms may also be obtained using "ssh -Q mac".

     1mMatch   22mIntroduces a conditional block.  If all of the criteria on the 1mMatch  22mline  are  satis‐
             fied,  the  keywords on the following lines override those set in the global section of
             the config file, until either another 1mMatch 22mline or the end of the file.  If a  keyword
             appears  in  multiple  1mMatch  22mblocks that are satisfied, only the first instance of the
             keyword is applied.

             The arguments to 1mMatch 22mare one or more criteria-pattern pairs or one of the single  to‐
             ken  criteria: 1mAll22m, which matches all criteria, or 1mInvalid-User22m, which matches when the
             requested user-name does not match any known account.  The available criteria are 1mUser22m,
             1mGroup22m, 1mHost22m, 1mLocalAddress22m, 1mLocalPort22m, 1mVersion22m, 1mRDomain22m, and 1mAddress 22m(with 1mRDomain  22mrep‐
             resenting the 8;;man:rdomain(4)4mrdomain24m(4)8;; on which the connection was received).

             The  match  patterns may consist of single entries or comma-separated lists and may use
             the wildcard and negation operators described in the  “PATTERNS”  section  of  8;;man:ssh_config(5)4mssh_con‐0m
             4mfig24m(5)8;;.

             The patterns in an 1mAddress 22mcriteria may additionally contain addresses to match in CIDR
             address/masklen  format,  such  as  192.0.2.0/24  or 2001:db8::/32.  Note that the mask
             length provided must be consistent with the address - it is an error to specify a  mask
             length  that  is  too long for the address or one with bits set in this host portion of

             1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand22m, 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommandUser22m, 1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile22m,
             1mBanner22m,  1mCASignatureAlgorithms22m,  1mChannelTimeout22m,  1mChrootDirectory22m, 1mClientAliveCountMax22m,
             1mClientAliveInterval22m,   1mDenyGroups22m,   1mDenyUsers22m,   1mDisableForwarding22m,    1mExposeAuthInfo22m,
             1mForceCommand22m,    1mGatewayPorts22m,    1mGSSAPIAuthentication22m,    1mHostbasedAcceptedAlgorithms22m,
             1mHostbasedAuthentication22m, 1mHostbasedUsesNameFromPacketOnly22m, 1mIgnoreRhosts22m, 1mInclude22m, 1mIPQoS22m,
             1mKbdInteractiveAuthentication22m,    1mKerberosAuthentication22m,    1mLogLevel22m,     1mMaxAuthTries22m,
             1mMaxSessions22m,      1mPAMServiceName22m,     1mPasswordAuthentication22m,     1mPermitEmptyPasswords22m,
             1mPermitListen22m,  1mPermitOpen22m,  1mPermitRootLogin22m,  1mPermitTTY22m,  1mPermitTunnel22m,   1mPermitUserRC22m,
             1mPubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms22m,  1mPubkeyAuthentication22m,  1mPubkeyAuthOptions22m,  1mRefuseConnection22m,
             1mRekeyLimit22m, 1mRevokedKeys22m, 1mRDomain22m, 1mSetEnv22m,  1mStreamLocalBindMask22m,  1mStreamLocalBindUnlink22m,

     1mMaxAuthTries0m
             Specifies the maximum number of authentication attempts permitted per connection.  Once
             the number of failures reaches half this value, additional failures  are  logged.   The
             default is 6.

     1mMaxSessions0m

             permitted per network connection.  Multiple sessions may be established by clients that
             support connection multiplexing.  Setting 1mMaxSessions 22mto  1  will  effectively  disable

             or to the wildcard address.  By default, sshd binds the forwarding server to the  loop‐
             back  address  and  sets  the  hostname  part  of  the  4mDISPLAY24m environment variable to
             1mlocalhost22m.  This prevents remote hosts from connecting to the proxy display.   However,
             some  older  X11 clients may not function with this configuration.  1mX11UseLocalhost 22mmay
             be set to 1mno 22mto specify that the forwarding server should be bound to the wildcard  ad‐
             dress.  The argument must be 1myes 22mor 1mno22m.  The default is 1myes22m.

     1mXAuthLocation0m
             Specifies  the  full pathname of the 8;;man:xauth(1)4mxauth24m(1)8;; program, or 1mnone 22mto not use one.  The de‐
             fault is 4m/usr/bin/xauth24m.

1mTIME FORMATS0m
     8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;; command-line arguments and configuration file options that  specify  time  may  be  ex‐
     pressed  using  a sequence of the form: 4mtime24m[4mqualifier24m], where 4mtime24m is a positive integer value
     and 4mqualifier24m is one of the following:

           ⟨1mnone22m⟩  seconds
           1ms 22m| 1mS   22mseconds
           1mm 22m| 1mM   22mminutes
           1mh 22m| 1mH   22mhours
           1md 22m| 1mD   22mdays
           1mw 22m| 1mW   22mweeks

     Each member of the sequence is added together to calculate the total time value.

     Time format examples:

           600     600 seconds (10 minutes)
           10m     10 minutes
           1h30m   1 hour 30 minutes (90 minutes)

1mTOKENS0m
     Arguments to some keywords can make use of tokens, which are expanded at runtime.   Tokens  are
     expanded  without quoting or escaping of shell characters.  It is the administrator's responsi‐
     bility to ensure they are safe in the context of their use.

     The supported tokens in 1msshd_config 22mare:

           %%    A literal ‘%’.
           %C    Identifies the connection endpoints, containing four space-separated values: client
                 address, client port number, server address, and server port number.
           %D    The routing domain in which the incoming connection was received.
           %F    The fingerprint of the CA key.
           %f    The fingerprint of the key or certificate.
           %h    The home directory of the user.
           %i    The key ID in the certificate.
           %K    The base64-encoded CA key.
           %k    The base64-encoded key or certificate for authentication.
           %s    The serial number of the certificate.
           %T    The type of the CA key.
           %t    The key or certificate type.
           %U    The numeric user ID of the target user.
           %u    The username.

     1mAgentSocketPath 22maccepts the tokens %%, %h, %U, and %u.

     1mAuthorizedKeysCommand 22maccepts the tokens %%, %C, %D, %f, %h, %k, %t, %U, and %u.

     1mAuthorizedKeysFile 22maccepts the tokens %%, %h, %U, and %u.

     1mAuthorizedPrincipalsCommand 22maccepts the tokens %%, %C, %D, %F, %f, %h, %i, %K, %k, %s, %T,  %t,
     %U, and %u.

     1mAuthorizedPrincipalsFile 22maccepts the tokens %%, %h, %U, and %u.

     1mChrootDirectory 22maccepts the tokens %%, %h, %U, and %u.

     1mRoutingDomain 22maccepts the token %D.

             Contains  configuration  data  for 8;;man:sshd(8)4msshd24m(8)8;;.  This file should be writable by root only,
             but it is recommended (though not necessary) that it be world-readable.
